# Current implementation contracts and acceptance

This is the current specification for the new federation release. Each contract and criterion appears once with its canonical IDs. All are planned obligations, not passing implementation results. C0/A1/B1/H1/M1/M2/S1 name exact hashes captured in each fixture manifest.

## 1. autonomous local execution

FR-MCP-174 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-001 / TEST-MCP-222. Phase: Ph2. Workflows: U02, U03, U06.

Every node, including the hub, performs authorized local business operations and persists results without hub connectivity.

Local request routing binds immutable ProjectId, NodeId and Branch to one DbContext and branch write gate. Dolt-mode domain requests never invoke LocalProxy forwarding or wait for the hub. Existing local authentication remains mandatory; federation reference-token introspection is not a dependency of local work. Result fields distinguish local persistence, version commit and publication.

- **NodeWorksWithHubUnavailable** (`ac-NodeWorksWithHubUnavailable`): Given A/main=C0 and the hub link is down, when A changes TODO T1.title from old to local, then the local API succeeds, a local reread returns local, and no hub request or history commit occurs.
- **HubUsesSameLocalExecution** (`ac-HubUsesSameLocalExecution`): Given H/main=C0 and the gateway is stopped, when H edits T1.title, then H persists it locally while remote/main remains C0.
- **OfflineLocalReadAfterWrite** (`ac-OfflineLocalReadAfterWrite`): Given the prior offline edit, when the application and Dolt restart, then T1.title remains local and main remains C0 until an explicit version commit.

## 2. explicit version commits and publication boundary

FR-MCP-175 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-002 / TEST-MCP-223. Phase: Ph4. Workflows: U02, U07, U09.

Only an explicit version-history commit triggers publication; drafts and SQL saves remain local. Commit retries recover the same history identity.

POST /qbrainai/federation/projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits accepts requestId UUID, expectedHead, expectedWorkingSet, leaseFence, author and message. Success is 201 with commitHash and publicationState=committed_locally. Persist requestId in the Dolt commit trailer. Retry returns the original hash. Head/fingerprint/fence mismatch is HTTP409 with head_changed/working_set_changed/lease_lost. SaveChanges and control.poll never create version commits.

- **SaveDoesNotPublish** (`ac-SaveDoesNotPublish`): Given main=C0 and remote=C0, when SaveChanges persists T1.title=draft, then main and remote stay C0 and no publication intent is emitted.
- **VersionCommitTriggersSync** (`ac-VersionCommitTriggersSync`): Given that draft and a valid preview, when commit request R1 succeeds, then main=A1, the reply says committed_locally, and one recoverable publication intent targets A1.
- **HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft** (`ac-HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft`): Given B has a draft and desired head A1, when B polls, then outcome=waiting_local_work, B/main=C0 and the draft value is unchanged.
- **OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart** (`ac-OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart`): Given A1 committed while disconnected and a crash before intent persistence, when A restarts, then history scanning rediscovers A1 exactly once and publishes it after reconnect.

## 3. logical project enrollment and initial clone

FR-MCP-176 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-003 / TEST-MCP-224. Phase: Ph2/Ph5. Workflows: U01.

Nodes enroll a logical project under immutable shared identity while retaining host-local paths and refusing destructive clones.

Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.

ProjectEnrollment stores ProjectId UUID, NodeId, ownerSubjectId, normalized local path, schemaVersion and subscriptions. POST /qbrainai/federation/enroll accepts an authenticated pre-provisioned node client plus operator-authorized owner binding. Body ProjectId must be allowed by token scope fed.project.{ProjectId}.enroll and durable membership. Paths stay host-local; no default-workspace fallback. A nonempty clone destination returns409 target_not_empty.

Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.

- **DifferentHostPathsSameProject** (`ac-DifferentHostPathsSameProject`): Given LAB path /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer and LEGION path F:/github/McpServer, when both enroll as ProjectId Atlas, then both reference Atlas and retain their distinct local paths.
- **CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget** (`ac-CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget`): Given target has TODO X, when clone is requested, then409 target_not_empty leaves X and all target files unchanged.
- **UnauthorizedProjectDenied** (`ac-UnauthorizedProjectDenied`): Given node A has only Atlas membership, when it enrolls or clones SecretProject, then403 unauthorized_project returns no rows, objects or project existence details.
- **PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics** (`ac-PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics`): Given Atlas is discoverable but A has a nonempty destination, when each plugin selects Atlas and attempts enrollment/clone, then it displays ProjectId, selected branch and409 target_not_empty with remediation; no database is overwritten and no different project is selected.

## 4. branches across server and plugin context

FR-MCP-177 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-004 / TEST-MCP-225. Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U08, U12.

First-release project branches support isolated work, explicit sharing and reviewed merge; session selection never leaks between connections.

Branch APIs create/list/select/merge using ProjectId, branch and sessionId. Each pooled connection is opened for an explicit branch and verified before use. Merge accepts expectedSourceHead and expectedTargetHead; stale values yield409 head_changed. Reserved refs upload/, integration/ and review/ are inaccessible to ordinary editing credentials. Branch deletion fails409 branch_busy while leases, reviews or recovery pins reference it.

- **PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch** (`ac-PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch`): Given main T1.title=main and feature/search T1.title=feature, when alternating pooled reads run100 times, then each returns only its selected value.
- **FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged** (`ac-FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged`): Given main=C0 and feature/search=F1, when F1 publishes, then remote feature=F1 and all main heads remain C0.
- **BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads** (`ac-BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads`): Given a preview for main=C0 and feature=F1 but feature advances to F2, when merge submits the old preview, then409 head_changed creates no commit and changes no ref.

## 5. bidirectional committed-history exchange

FR-MCP-178 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-005 / TEST-MCP-226. Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U03, U04, U08.

Exchange committed history bidirectionally through guarded publication, preserving every accepted ancestor and the hub independent working copy.

Node upload authority is limited to its candidate namespace in an isolated upload repository. POST /qbrainai/federation/publication/accept accepts projectId, branch, requestId, candidateHead, expectedPublishedHead and hubEpoch. Gateway validates authorization, ancestry, schema and domain invariants before the sole fenced publisher advances the public ref without force. Token validation occurs at the gateway; native Dolt remotesapi is loopback-only and never trusts a node bearer token directly. Transport/procedure enforcement is a Ph0 proof gate.

- **ThreeWriterCleanConvergence** (`ac-ThreeWriterCleanConvergence`): Given C0 contains T1.title=old,T1.description=old,T2.priority=low, when A1 changes title=A, B1 changes description=B and H1 changes T2.priority=high, then merges M1(A1,B1), M2(M1,H1) converge all heads to M2 with values A,B,high and all three commits in ancestry.
- **HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote** (`ac-HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote`): Given H has an uncommitted title draft at C0, when A publishes A1, then remote=A1, H remains C0 with its draft, and B can accept A1.
- **ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories** (`ac-ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories`): Given A1 and B1 descend from C0, when both accept requests expect C0, then one succeeds and the other receives409 head_changed; after merge M1 publishes, both A1 and B1 remain ancestors.

## 6. hub control table and polling

FR-MCP-179 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-006 / TEST-MCP-227. Phase: Ph5. Workflows: U02, U06, U09, U15.

Use a durable hub subscription table with polling, generation and worker fencing, plus a fresh hub epoch after restore.

SyncSubscription key=(NodeId,ProjectId,Branch) contains HubEpoch UUID, PublishedHead, PublishedGeneration int64, DesiredGeneration int64, ReportedGeneration int64, WorkerEpoch int64, AcceptedHead, Outcome and timestamps. POST control/poll is read-only. POST control/report includes all epochs and observed generation; stale worker=409 stale_worker_epoch, stale hub=409 hub_epoch_changed. Poll every30s with20% jitter; commit/reconnect/on-demand wake immediately. Backoff1s doubling to60s. Generation ordering is valid only within HubEpoch. Restore generates a new non-reused random epoch before listeners reopen.

- **PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge** (`ac-PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge`): Given desired=7 and reported=6, when poll runs twice, then both responses request7 and stored reported remains6.
- **AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest** (`ac-AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest`): Given desired becomes8 while report7 is in flight, when report7 arrives, then reported=7, desired=8 and the subscription remains pending.
- **MissedNotificationReconciles** (`ac-MissedNotificationReconciles`): Given remote=A1 but control still names C0 after a crash, when reconciliation runs, then it records A1 and advances desired generation without producing another commit.
- **HubRestoreFromOlderBackup** (`ac-HubRestoreFromOlderBackup`): Given a node remembers epoch E1 generation90 and the hub restores a backup at generation40, when the hub reopens, then epoch E2 differs from E1; E1 reports fail409 hub_epoch_changed and no head is force-reset. Node A1 is retained until verified ancestry recovery republishes missing history.

## 7. reviewed conflicts and valid merges

FR-MCP-180 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-007 / TEST-MCP-228. Phase: Ph6/Ph7. Workflows: U05, U07, U08.

Conflicts and invalid merges preserve valid live data, require authorized review and remain visible with ageing while unrelated publication continues.

Review record key=ReviewId UUID; fields ProjectId,Branch,baseHeads[],localHead,incomingHead,candidateRef,conflictingCells[],validationErrors[],createdUtc,lastNotifiedUtc,resolution,actor. GET conflicts and status expose it. Resolve binds exact heads and returns409 stale_review if changed. Safe TODO policy: identical concurrent values collapse; edits to different cells may merge only if invariants pass; duplicate immutable child IDs deduplicate only when bytes agree. Status, priority, title, description, dependency deletions and same-cell disagreements always require review; no timestamp last-writer-wins. Notify immediately in status and durable operator inbox; warn at15min, escalate at24h, repeat at most hourly; no email/Slack sent implicitly. Same-branch dependent commits wait; unrelated branches/projects continue.

- **SameCellConflictNeedsReview** (`ac-SameCellConflictNeedsReview`): Given base priority=low, A1 priority=high and B1 priority=medium, when B integrates A1, then needs_review shows low/medium/high, B/main remains B1 and no public ref is overwritten.
- **DeleteUpdateNeedsReview** (`ac-DeleteUpdateNeedsReview`): Given A1 deletes T1 and B1 edits T1.title, when histories merge, then needs_review retains B1 and the deleted/edited alternatives for review.
- **CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation** (`ac-CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation`): Given separate commits add T1 dependsOn T2 and T2 dependsOn T1, when Dolt merges without cell conflicts, then domain validation records dependency_cycle and leaves the prior valid live head unchanged.
- **StaleReviewRejected** (`ac-StaleReviewRejected`): Given a resolution preview binds local=B1 and incoming=A1, when incoming advances to A2, then resolve returns409 stale_review with no merge commit.
- **ReviewAgeVisible** (`ac-ReviewAgeVisible`): Given unresolved needs_review at12:00, when the clock reaches12:15, then plugins/status and the operator inbox show warning with ReviewId and age900s; at24h severity is critical, with at most one repeat per hour.
- **UnrelatedPublicationContinues** (`ac-UnrelatedPublicationContinues`): Given Atlas/main is blocked by review R1, when Atlas/feature publishes F2 and another project publishes X1, then both succeed while Atlas/main remains unchanged.
- **SafeTodoMergeRules** (`ac-SafeTodoMergeRules`): Given A changes title and B changes description with no domain violation, when merge runs, then both values survive; competing priority or completion edits produce needs_review instead of choosing a timestamp winner.

## 8. recovery without lost or repeated work

FR-MCP-181 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-008 / TEST-MCP-229. Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U06, U07, U09, U15.

Recover synchronization, receipts and restored hub state without losing local work, inventing success or replaying business effects.

Server: durable operation resume/status/safe cancellation. Plugin: expose resume, status and cancel with completed-versus-pending effects; never claim cancellation reverses published history.

OperationReceipt binds requestId, node, project, branch, hubEpoch, candidate/result hashes and outcome. Durable refs pin candidates/reviews before receipt completion. Worker claims are fenced by WorkerEpoch; reconnect never trusts stored generation across HubEpoch. Fetch may advance remote-tracking refs, never dirty live refs. Restore first disables ingress, restores compatible data/control/audit checkpoints, creates new epoch, then re-advertises verified heads; node-held missing commits are uploaded and ancestry-validated before normal synchronization resumes.

Server: durable operation resume/status/safe cancellation. Plugin: expose resume, status and cancel with completed-versus-pending effects; never claim cancellation reverses published history.

HubRestoreFromOlderBackup is first owned by Ph5 (epoch/remote/control), extended by Ph6 (integration/review/audit resend), and repeated as isolated real-host acceptance in Ph8. Restore is tested, never assumed from successful backup creation.

- **LostPushAckDoesNotDuplicateCommit** (`ac-LostPushAckDoesNotDuplicateCommit`): Given remote accepted A1 and reply was lost, when request R1 retries, then it returns A1 and the existing receipt; no A2 commit is created.
- **OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess** (`ac-OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess`): Given worker epoch changes4 to5, when epoch4 reports success, then409 stale_worker_epoch leaves current receipt and desired state unchanged.
- **DirtyBranchDefersApply** (`ac-DirtyBranchDefersApply`): Given B/main=C0 with title=draft, when A1 is fetched, then outcome=waiting_local_work, main stays C0 and title remains draft; at15min status/inbox shows the age warning.
- **IncompatibleSchemaDoesNotApply** (`ac-IncompatibleSchemaDoesNotApply`): Given B supports schema1 and incoming S1 requires schema2, when sync runs, then409 incompatible_schema leaves B's live data/head unchanged and records the required version.
- **PluginRecoveryControls** (`ac-PluginRecoveryControls`): Given operation R1 published A1 but its local reply was lost, when a plugin resumes, reads status and requests cancellation, then it shows publishedHead=A1 and a durable cancellation outcome for remaining work; it never claims A1 was rolled back or creates a second commit.

## 9. collision-resistant and preserved identity

FR-MCP-182 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-009 / TEST-MCP-230. Phase: Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U01, U10, U14.

Prevent generated-ID collisions, preserve permanent legacy aliases, detect duplicate work and atomically reserve human-assigned IDs.

Server: provenance, scoped aliases, collision evidence and reservation outcomes. Plugin: expose provenance/collision diagnostics and the authorized resolution path without rewriting historical references.

Generated IDs use immutable two-character creator tags and durable branch-independent sequences with per-family grammar fixed in Ph0. Alias key=(ProjectId,OriginNodeId,EntityKind,LegacyId) maps permanently to CanonicalId; ambiguous unqualified lookup returns409 ambiguous_legacy_id. Historical text/commits are not rewritten. Migration duplicate candidates use normalized title/description/dependency features, returning similarity score plus evidence, never auto-merging. Human ID reservations are unique(ProjectId,EntityKind,HumanId) at the hub, bound to node/requestId. Offline nodes use generated provisional IDs; an unreserved human ID is not publishable.

Server: provenance, scoped aliases, collision evidence and reservation outcomes. Plugin: expose provenance/collision diagnostics and the authorized resolution path without rewriting historical references.

- **TwoNodesCreateDistinctIds** (`ac-TwoNodesCreateDistinctIds`): Given tags LA and LG and both counters start1, when both create a TODO, then generated IDs differ and both records survive reconciliation.
- **BranchRevertDoesNotReuseSequence** (`ac-BranchRevertDoesNotReuseSequence`): Given LA allocated sequence42, when main reverts and another branch creates a record, then its sequence is greater than42.
- **LegacyCollisionPreservesReferences** (`ac-LegacyCollisionPreservesReferences`): Given LAB and LEGION have different entities named TODO-7, when migration resolves the collision, then scoped aliases resolve each original identity and every relational reference follows its reviewed canonical mapping; historical text remains byte-identical.
- **LegacyIdsRemainValid** (`ac-LegacyIdsRemainValid`): Given existing IMPL-UNITGREEN-001 and old TODO references, when imported and read by their original IDs, then they resolve through permanent aliases without rewriting commits, PR text, session logs, memories or documents.
- **DifferentIdsSameTodoDetected** (`ac-DifferentIdsSameTodoDetected`): Given LAB TODO-7 and LEGION TODO-91 share normalized title Fix login, description and dependency set, when migration plan runs, then it emits a duplicate candidate with both IDs and evidence; until explicit review, neither is merged or deleted.
- **SimultaneousHumanIdReservation** (`ac-SimultaneousHumanIdReservation`): Given human ID IMPL-UNITGREEN-001 is unreserved, when two nodes reserve it concurrently, then exactly one receives201 and the other409 human_id_reserved; retry by the winning requestId returns the same reservation.
- **OfflineHumanIdPublicationDenied** (`ac-OfflineHumanIdPublicationDenied`): Given an offline-created provisional TODO requesting an unreserved human ID, when it reconnects and publishes, then409 human_id_unreserved retains the local record until reservation or reviewed alias resolution.
- **PluginIdentityDiagnostics** (`ac-PluginIdentityDiagnostics`): Given LAB TODO-7 and LEGION TODO-91 are a duplicate candidate, when each plugin opens identity review, then both origin IDs, canonical/provisional IDs, similarity evidence and reservation outcome are visible; no alias or row changes before an authorized decision.

## 10. first-party plugin federation contract

FR-MCP-183 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010 / TEST-MCP-231. Phase: Ph4/Ph7. Workflows: U01, U02, U05, U07, U08, U11, U12, U13, U14, U15.

Expose consistent typed federation, review, identity, audit, migration and maintenance workflows through every first-party plugin.

All plugins call typed server/client/MCP/REPL contracts; no raw SQL/CLI fallback. Status DTO includes projectId, branch, localHead, publishedHead, observedUtc, dirty, ahead, behind, publicationState, incomingTarget, connectivity, reviewCount, oldestReviewAgeSeconds, waitingLocalWorkAgeSeconds, auditPendingCount, hubEpoch, workerEpoch. Capability contract version1 is negotiated; unknown version=409 unsupported_contract. Administrative maintenance.preflight/attest/status and migration commands share the same typed service as Nuke. Stable error envelope={code, message, requestId, projectId, branch, retryable, details}; status codes are locked in the technical contract appendix.

Technical contract appendix (TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010): all below routes are under /qbrainai/federation unless the commits route specifies the project/branch path. Every mutation requires requestId UUID and authenticated subject; node network requests additionally carry the project-scoped reference token. Responses carry contractVersion=1 and the stable error envelope. Path/body ProjectId mismatch is403 unauthorized_project. No endpoint accepts credentials in URL, argv or persisted receipts.

Read/status routes: GET capabilities returns200 {contractVersion,capabilities}; GET projects/{projectId}/status returns200 the status DTO; GET projects/{projectId}/branches returns200 {items:[{name,head,dirty,publishedHead}]}; GET conflicts and GET conflicts/{reviewId} return200 review records filtered by membership. POST control/poll returns200 {hubEpoch,subscriptions}; reads never acknowledge work. POST control/report validates observed generation and worker epoch, returns200 the durable receipt or409 the named fence error. Poll/report use control scope; reads use read scope.

Mutation routes: POST enroll returns201 the enrollment (or200 the same idempotent enrollment); POST projects/{projectId}/branches creates201 {branch,head}; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/select returns200 {sessionId,branch,head} after local lease validation; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits returns201 {commitHash,publicationState}, or200 the same commit on retry. POST publication/accept returns200 {requestId,hubEpoch,publishedHead,publishedGeneration,receiptId} only after the guarded ref update is durable. POST branches/merge and POST conflicts/{reviewId}/resolve bind expected heads and return201 the new commit; a conflict returns202 {outcome:needs_review,reviewId} while the live head stays unchanged. Share/merge/publication require publish scope plus branch permission. Enrollment requires enroll scope and the operator owner-binding approval.

POST audit/batches accepts {requestId,projectId,records:[AuditRecord]}, returns200 {receipts:[{originNodeId,recordId,payloadHash,outcome,receivedUtc}]}, and requires audit scope. Every record must match the token/project and batch ProjectId. Any invalid record rejects the whole batch before insert. Exact duplicate is already_received; payload mismatch is409 audit_id_conflict. POST ids/reservations accepts {requestId,projectId,entityKind,humanId,nodeId}, requires publish scope and returns201 the reservation or200 its exact retry; another owner gets409 human_id_reserved. POST maintenance/preflight and POST maintenance/attest, GET maintenance/status and POST migration/{plan|dry-run|run|resume|verify|export-project|export-todos|cutover|abort}, GET migration/status are operator-only local service operations. They are exposed through typed clients and Nuke, never public node-admin capabilities. A long migration returns202 {migrationId,status}; status/verify return200 a receipt, and a denied readiness check never performs cutover.

Stable failure mapping:401 invalid_token;403 unauthorized_project;409 head_changed, working_set_changed, lease_lost, branch_busy, stale_review, stale_worker_epoch, hub_epoch_changed, ambiguous_legacy_id, human_id_reserved, human_id_unreserved, target_not_empty, maintenance_not_ready, migration_source_changed, migration_verification_failed, incompatible_schema, unsupported_contract, publication_required, request_id_conflict, audit_id_conflict and waiting_local_work (the last also a 200 outcome in poll/report; see outcome fields);422 secret_detected, dependency_cycle and unsupported_provider;501 unsupported_capability;503 identity_unavailable or remote_unavailable. TLS rejection produces the local transport code tls_peer_untrusted with no HTTP response and no request sent. Missing required fields return400 invalid_request. Missing authorized resources return404 not_found; project authorization precedes existence disclosure. Malformed/unsupported token is401; valid token lacking project rights is403.

Outcome fields are not HTTP errors: committed_locally, already_received, already_applied, waiting_local_work and needs_review remain visible through200 status/report responses (already_applied is the migration-journal idempotency outcome for a rerun completed batch, distinct from the audit-ledger already_received). A requested live mutation blocked by drafts returns409 waiting_local_work; an integration that durably creates review returns202 needs_review. dependency_cycle is a validationErrors entry on that review as well as422 for a directly invalid local mutation. retryable=true is restricted to transient503/transport failures; all stale-head/fence/review errors require reread and a fresh validated action. Idempotent retries with the same requestId but different payload return409 request_id_conflict. No automatic retry creates a different commit.

Test fixtures capture actual content hashes as symbols C0,A1,B1,H1,M1,M2,S1 rather than hardcoding unstable engine hashes. Each symbol is immutable within the run manifest. Given/When/Then compares exact hash equality, specified parent sets, row values, status codes and error codes against that manifest; a successful result must never be inferred solely from an empty queue. Capture UTC timestamps and a fake clock for exact15-minute/24-hour age boundaries. All plan phase IDs use Ph0-Ph8; priority values remain separate.

Plugin completeness is checked by PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics, PluginRecoveryControls, PluginIdentityDiagnostics, PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial, PluginEffectBoundary and PluginEditingOwnership in their mapped contracts. Ph7 owns their plugin bindings; earlier phases own server behavior. Standalone and explicit DirectProxy compatibility remain under FR-MCP-077/TR-MCP-FED-001; this does not reinstate versioned LocalProxy forwarding.

- **EveryPluginUsesSameContract** (`ac-EveryPluginUsesSameContract`): Given one fixture for commit R1, conflict R2 and migration R3, when each installed first-party plugin calls its wrapper, then normalized IDs, heads, error codes and audit agent identity match the typed client result.
- **OldServerReportsUnsupportedCapability** (`ac-OldServerReportsUnsupportedCapability`): Given server lacks federation contract1, when a plugin invokes commit, then unsupported_contract is shown and no raw SQL or shell fallback executes.
- **ReconnectRevalidatesContext** (`ac-ReconnectRevalidatesContext`): Given a cached leaseFence4 and session branch feature, when reconnect discovers fence5, then the plugin retains visible context but refuses writes with lease_lost until reacquired.

### Required fixture coverage

Ph3 migration fixtures cover every classified project domain and its child/link graph, soft-deleted rows, multiple projects, decimal/UTC/binary/Unicode edge cases, promoted session snapshots, audit records, derived-index rebuild and inert operational metadata. ResumeAfterBatchCommit injects death after target-batch commit before acknowledgement. FailedVerifyCannotCutover additionally tests death before provider mapping switch and after switch before reopening: recovery opens exactly one verified provider, retains source bytes and never loses Dolt-only writes. Dry-run and failed verification cannot alter source or routing. Ph6 repeats these invariants for reviewed joins.

Path fixtures retain syntax-aware Windows/UNC/Linux normalization and containment, no host-native reinterpretation of a foreign path, and backed-up transactional source rekey where required. Session fixtures preserve every field/child, PlanFile/TodoId, unknown/missing-session behavior and source sanitization parity. Memory fixtures preserve IDs, scope, ownership, versions and soft deletion. Configuration fixtures retain hub-admin requirement-layer policy, report drift, and keep RunAs/paths/tunnels host-local. These are applicable migration/security constraints, not additional historical feature work.

9	The logical peers H, A and B must independently edit and commit the same logical project's data, exchange committed histories through the hub, preserve uncommitted work and branches, and review conflicts without pull requests. Add Dolt as a fourth supported database and provide a safe migration tool from SQLite, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. Existing providers and explicit DirectProxy remain supported. The second node is the isolated FED-ATLAS-B test peer; real-host acceptance uses LAB and LEGION, with the three-peer fixture provisioned in Ph0.
10	
11	Success is demonstrated by every workflow U01-U15, every linked FR/TR/TEST criterion, all supported provider regressions and three-system restart/recovery tests. An empty control table is insufficient proof: compare accepted commit ancestry, project data and branch state, including pending drafts/reviews. Source-code Git, arbitrary file synchronization, PRs, automatic hub election, live cross-provider CDC and concurrent independent schema migrations are outside this release.
12	
13	## 2. Fastest dependency sequence
14	
15	Phase identifiers are Ph0 through Ph8; they do not denote priority levels.
16	
17	1. Ph0: prove Dolt/EF10/provider/remote fit before investing in integration.
18	2. Ph1: add fourth provider and separate schema migration assembly; preserve original providers.
19	3. Ph2: split project-versioned and operational storage, branch-scoped access and editing ownership.
20	4. Ph3: deliver seed migration, audit-backfill preparation and verified all-domain project recovery export; keep targets isolated.
21	5. Ph4: expose explicit commits, branch/history/diff and local publication intent.
22	6. Ph5: implement enrollment, guarded remote publication and the hub table/poller.
23	7. Ph6: implement safe receiving, reviewed merges, join migration and end-to-end crash/restore recovery.
24	8. Ph7: expose complete client/MCP/REPL/plugin workflows and user-visible status.
25	9. Ph8: run two-real-host acceptance plus a named three-logical-peer fixture, then prepare a staged lab cutover under DEPLOY HOLD.
26	
27	Prepare test fixtures, DTO/API documentation and plugin contract fixtures during earlier phases where independent, but do not move unfinished implementation past a Byrd gate. Provider feasibility, not old forwarding fixes, is now the critical path. Reuse existing identity, diagnostics, provider abstractions, audit and typed clients; replace forwarding/command-replay paths only for versioned projects.
28	
29	## 3. Source-control and donor handling
30	
31	Create an isolated integration worktree from the current accepted develop when implementation is authorized. Suggested branch `integration/federation-dolt-20261110`; use separate small phase PRs against it. Preserve all existing worktrees and unrelated working-tree edits. Do not create or clean worktrees merely to write this plan.
32	
33	The prior PR83/P1.5 work is a donor only for applicable security, identity, cross-platform path and regression fixes. Verify each current diff and test before porting. Do not merge old backfill, forwarding, read-switch or custom database synchronization machinery wholesale. C4 p4/*, namespace/analyzer work and historical worktree cleanup are not dependencies. Preserve explicit existing legacy modes through their named regression contracts; they do not authorize LocalProxy forwarding for versioned projects.
34	
35	## 4. Byrd gate contract
36	
37	For each small slice, first define the acceptance cases, fixtures and negative controls. Prove tests pass against controlled mocks and fail against deliberately wrong behavior. Then run the same contract against the missing/incorrect real implementation to record red, implement the smallest behavior, and refactor to green. Mocks must not simply return the expected result without testing the orchestration boundary.
38	
39	Use targeted `./build.ps1 TestGroups --test-groups '<project>:<class>' --test-run-id '<phase-slice>'` after changes. At each phase exit run the entire current-plus-prior unit suite once with `./build.ps1 Test`, requiring zero failures and zero skips. `./build.ps1 Compile` and `./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability` are mandatory gate commands. Add real-container integration tests where a mock cannot prove SQL, migration, locking or remote semantics. Do not broaden/repeat a passing gate without changes or new evidence requiring it. Receipts include SHA/tree state, image/package versions, commands, TRX, fail/skip counts, AC mapping and negative controls.
40	
41	The proposed test-class names below are implementation targets, not claims they exist today. Register new projects/classes in Nuke discovery as part of their owning phase. Do not add skipped placeholders for later phases; keep deferred coverage in requirements/TODO state.
42	
43	Retain the operator's complete phase-exit gate on both LAB and LEGION: Nuke Test, MigrationIntegrationTests, the full Build.Tests suite, and ValidateTraceability at the same accepted head. Test currently excludes Build.Tests; do not infer its coverage from a green Test receipt. Ph0 records the complete discovered Build.Tests class inventory and its Nuke TestGroups invocation; every listed class and test must execute, with zero failures and zero skips. MigrationIntegrationTests and the new TestFederationProviders suite are complementary and neither replaces the other. Keep unit, integration and build-suite receipts distinct and run the full set once per final phase head, repeating only after changes or failed gates.
44	
45	Add Nuke target `TestFederationProviders` with the planned command `./build.ps1 TestFederationProviders --providers sqlite,postgresql,sqlserver,dolt --test-run-id '<phase>-providers'`. It is not an existing command today. Ph0 records exact PostgreSQL/SQL Server/Dolt image versions and digests and the SQLite package version; Ph1 implements the target and refuses missing/unhealthy containers as a gate failure, never a skip. Every Ph1-Ph8 exit requires both the full unit gate and this real-provider/remote suite with zero failures and zero skips. Container-dependent classes are registered only in TestFederationProviders and excluded from Test by category at discovery, never runtime skipping. Receipts include image digests and environment readiness evidence.
46	
47	## 5. Ph0: feasibility and exact dependency selection
48	
49	Deliver a version-pinned compatibility receipt and license/dependency record for Dolt and the MySQL-protocol EF provider and driver selected under B1. Use current net10.0/EF10.0.0 as the baseline. Read the dependency compliance rules before additions. Existing Dolt EF samples establish possibility, not compatibility.
50	
51	Prove on LAB Linux and LEGION native Windows against real databases (containers where appropriate): full current model creation; representative CRUD/LINQ/raw SQL; concurrency tokens; transaction rollback; decimal/date/text/index/FK mappings; migrations; branch connection isolation; explicit SQL commit versus Dolt commit; merge conflicts/constraints; clean and dirty remote pushes; lost responses; authenticated project isolation; inability to bypass guarded publication through raw remote requests. Verify canonical-ref advancement and remote recovery under process death. Compare candidate clean merges against domain validators.
52	
53	Classes: `DoltProviderCompatibilityTests`, `DoltRemoteAuthorizationTests`, `DoltBranchIsolationTests`, `DoltCommitBoundaryTests`. Red conditions: unsupported mappings/query translation, ordinary SaveChanges creating history, pool branch leakage, unauthorized ref mutation or missing recovery guarantees. Green: all named contracts pass on pinned versions, no ad hoc provider fork or custom merge engine.
54	
55	Ph0 runs a disposable harness and records exact commands, digests, TRX and fail/skip counts. Ph1 carries the proven Ph0 contract assertions into maintained classes under TestFederationProviders and passes them at Ph1 exit. If Ph0 changes repository code, the full Test gate also applies at Ph0 exit; disposable prototypes do not become an undocumented production dependency.
56	
57	Ph0 exit consists of the following numbered **blocking outputs**. The implementation owner produces each evidence record; the operator accepts it, with independent HV by an agent family other than the author, assessing substantive accuracy/completeness. Each record stores owner, status (unproven/proven/accepted), evidence paths and dependent phases. Initial status for all B1-B12 is unproven. Every B1-B12 receipt has separate LAB and LEGION evidence rows; Windows is not inferred from Linux. Ph0 verifies the current-scope coverage index and binds each applicable acceptance criterion and workflow to its implementation phase. All must be accepted before Ph1 production integration begins; Ph0 prototypes remain disposable.
58	
59	1. B1: exact provider/driver/image versions, digests, licenses and all-four-provider fixture versions; LAB /var/lib/dolt mount and native LEGION hosting inventory. Verify actual Windows service name/account/executable/start/recovery policy, data ACLs and child-process lifecycle before accepting the proposed host. If absent or unsuitable, obtain approval for a concrete supported alternative (Ph1-Ph8).
60	2. B2: every entity, relationship, interactive/automatic writer and auto-updated column; session capture remains operational and only explicit promoted snapshots become versioned (Ph2-Ph8).
61	3. B3: full standalone McpDbContext versus Dolt-only project/control context topology, additive migration chains and cross-database soft-reference validators (Ph1-Ph3).
62	4. B4: exact ID grammar per generated/human-assigned family, legacy compatibility, sort/display, parser/plugin/traceability changes and restored allocator behavior (Ph2-Ph8).
63	5. B5: exact restored Duende 7.4 patch version and matching source-tag/API references, with issuance/introspection/revocation tests on that package (v8 documentation is insufficient); existing IdentityServer client-per-node/owner binding, reference tokens and scopes, gateway introspection/revocation, backend-only Dolt credentials, enforceable remote publication permissions and credential containment, worker-only remote procedures, gated worker live-branch mutation path and rotation/revocation (Ph2/Ph5-Ph8).
64	6. B6: real merge/constraint/conflict-transaction semantics, retained review evidence, safe conflict persistence including whether `dolt_allow_commit_conflicts` is needed, and unrelated-history behavior. Never enable unresolved conflicts on live project branches (Ph4-Ph6).
65	7. B7: single-author schema distribution, startup migration exclusion, expand/contract rules, mandatory pre-binary-swap draft disposition, all-local-branch attestation/fencing, offline old-schema commits and feature catch-up, worker protocol negotiation (Ph1/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6/Ph8).
66	8. B8: seed/join/recovery-export manifest, audit backfill, duplicate detection and permanent aliases, one common root, mandatory legacy-divergence review over B2-classified versioned columns after canonical normalization; reviewed scoped rules may expand to enumerated per-row decisions with no wildcard default. Include identity/deletion accounting, canonical hashes, immutable migration-commit plus final-main verification and closed-until-integrated cutover (Ph3 seed/export, Ph6 join, Ph8 acceptance).
67	9. B9: single writer ownership, write gate/fence transitions including every worker live-branch mutation, working-set hash API, requestId commit trailers and crash reconciliation (Ph2/Ph4-Ph6).
68	10. B10: measured fixture-scale storage/latency/history growth, resource budgets and explicit operating limits; no unsupported throughput/SLA claim (Ph1/Ph5/Ph8).
69	11. B11: polling/retry/stale-branch and15minute/24hour review-age thresholds, subscription-state schema and monotonic generation/epoch semantics (Ph5/Ph7).
70	12. B12: local/remote candidate/review refs, GC/retention, hub-restore epoch/reconciliation, network loopback isolation, named CA/pins and secret-safe receipts, plus secret-detection and disclosure response (Ph4-Ph8).
71	
72	If a maintained EF10-compatible provider is unavailable, report concrete options for approval; do not downgrade the repository silently. This plan is executable through Ph0 but is not implementation-ready for later slices until these evidence-dependent choices are locked.
73	
74	## 6. Ph1: fourth provider and schema migrations
75	
76	Requirements: FR-MCP-186. Extend `McpDatabaseProviderKind`, `McpDatabaseProviderFactory`, `McpDbContextFactory`, runtime options/configuration validation, health output and setup tooling with canonical `dolt`. Add `DoltMcpDatabaseProviderStrategy` and `QBrainAi.Storage.DoltMigrations`, with provider-specific snapshot/baseline. Never edit existing migrations; add migrations only where B3 requires. Include provider selections in build/package/admin surfaces. Exclude versioned project databases from automatic startup migration; standalone/control contexts retain their approved migration path.
77	
78	Classes: `DoltProviderResolutionTests`, `DoltMigrationTests`, `FourProviderContractTests`. Include VersionedProjectNotMigratedAtStartup in this owning phase. First prove unknown-provider rejection, unchanged defaults and distinct migration assembly selection. Real-provider tests cover empty database creation, baseline-to-next upgrade, interrupted startup/retry, idempotent reapplication, schema drift detection and application CRUD after upgrade. Test all original providers for regression. No production data copy in this phase.
79	
80	## 7. Ph2: project routing, data boundaries and editing ownership
81	
82	Requirements: FR-MCP-174,176,177,182,184,185,189. Add immutable ProjectId/local-path enrollment mapping, per-project provider selection, project and control contexts, full table classification, branch-scoped DbContext/query/index keys, local ID allocation and fenced edit leases. A versioned project's ordinary requests must never enter LocalProxy forwarding. Preserve DirectProxy behavior for explicit legacy configuration; no ambiguous combination on one project.
83	
84	Fold MCP-FEDIDENTITY-001 owner binding and user-management requirements into this phase. Audit/outbox storage remains unversioned, but its delivery obligation is hub-bound, not local-only. Define scoped permanent aliases and local provisional IDs; host paths and credentials remain local. Classes: `FederationLocalExecutionTests`, `ProjectBranchContextTests`, `FederationDataBoundaryTests`, `NodeTaggedIdentityTests`, `BranchEditLeaseTests`. Cases include BackgroundWritersDoNotDirtyVersionedBranch, SecondAgentLoggingNeedsNoLease, LegacyIdsRemainValid and LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected. Red: offline request waits for hub, cross-project row visible, secret or branchable audit in clone, duplicate IDs after branch/restart, pooled connection changes branch, or one agent commits another's work. Green: local read-after-write/restart, complete entity/writer classification, no branch/project leakage, safe expired-lease recovery and stable replicated IDs. Provider schema changes introduced here require migrations for each affected supported provider, not Dolt alone.
85	
86	LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected means admission after expiry/fence change is rejected and takeover waits for an already-admitted transaction; it does not demand aborting a transaction legitimately holding the gate through completion.
87	
88	## 8. Ph3: seed migration and project recovery export
89	
90	Requirements: FR-MCP-187, FR-MCP-182/184, FR-MCP-AUDIT-001 and the reconciled backfill contracts. Implement the shared migration planner, immutable source manifest, duplicate-candidate review, permanent alias mapping, seed-only run/resume/verify/status/abort and frozen-head Dolt-to-new-SQLite project export. Audit backfill preparation accounts for every historical TODO/generic audit row; actual hub delivery/receipt binding joins Ph5. Ph3 never invokes publication or reviewed join functionality that does not yet exist.
91	
92	Classes: MigrationPlannerTests, MigrationResumeTests, MigrationIdentityMappingTests, MigrationVerificationTests, ThreeProviderToDoltMigrationTests, TodoRecoveryExportTests and ProjectRecoveryExportTests. Reuse TEST-MCP-235's exact Given/When/Then cases. SeedPhaseRejectsJoin returns HTTP 501 unsupported_capability with no writes when mode=join is requested. ThreeSourceProviderRoundTrip covers SQLite,PostgreSQL,SQL Server fixtures; both live lab sources are SQLite. DoltTodoExportPreservesNewWrites proves a post-cutover TODO and its child/link/alias graph survive export while retained source bytes remain unchanged. FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains additionally proves every versioned domain, unpublished branch and dirty working set survives per-branch SQLite export plus the retained Dolt archive; operational stores are backed up at the same quiescence boundary and audit is reconciled. A missing domain or branch blocks routing changes. Same-work/different-ID candidates require review; never rewrite historical text references.
93	
94	Migration acceptance also covers multi-project separation, soft-deleted rows, decimal/UTC/binary/Unicode edge cases, complete promoted session graphs, hub-bound audit, derived-index rebuild and inert imported operational records. Inject death after target batch commit before acknowledgement, before provider switch and after switch before reopening. Dry-run and failed verification must preserve source bytes and active routing. Ph6 applies the same matrix to joins; source accounting and reviewed-main verification are separate checks.
95	
96	Exit: disposable seed migrations and verified recovery exports pass all four-provider gates. Keep source SQLite snapshots read-only. No live cutover, join commit, public-ref update or source deletion occurs. Join-specific cases remain planned for Ph6, not skipped tests in Ph3.
97	## 9. Ph4: explicit history commits and local publication intent
98	
99	Requirements: FR-MCP-175,177,183,184,189. Implement status/diff/history/commit preview, idempotent explicit commit, branch lifecycle and local unpublished-head scanning. No save hook implicitly creates Dolt history. A hub request cannot auto-commit drafts. Protect preview fingerprints, author provenance and branch edit ownership.
100	
101	Classes: `FederationCommitTests`, `FederationBranchLifecycleTests`, `PublicationIntentRecoveryTests`. Include CommitRetryReturnsSameHash, CommitPreviewBlocksSecret and StaleBranchReportedNotDeleted. Red: edits trigger sync, commit bundles unauthorized changes, restart loses an unreported commit, or fetched remote commits cause endless republishing. Green: durable explicit commit triggers exactly the needed sync intent, history reconstruction repairs crash windows without duplicate commits, feature publication does not merge main.
102	
103	## 10. Ph5: hub control table and publication
104	
105	Requirements: FR-MCP-176,178,179,181,182,184,185. Provision the hub shared remote separately from its local working copy. Implement enrollment and project/branch subscription, candidate upload/validation/acceptance, expected-head publication, SyncSubscription state-table migrations, polling/reporting, durable receipts, worker epochs and remote-head reconciliation. One row per subscription replaces command-message generations/leases/coalescing. Both nodes initiate communication; H's local worker uses the same authenticated gateway. Add existing IdentityServer clients/scopes, audit/batches ingestion with idempotent receipts, human-ID reservation, restore epoch and polling. Test AuditReachesHub, AuditRetryIdempotent, SimultaneousHumanIdReservation, SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink and HubRestoreFromOlderBackup. No native remote endpoint is exposed to node credentials.
106	
107	Classes: `FederationEnrollmentTests`, `FederationPublicationTests`, `FederationControlTableTests`, `FederationPollingTests`. Include LocalAppUserCannotPush, RevokedCredentialFailsFetchAndPublish and OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess. Red: node can publish unauthorized branch/project, hub drafts block publication, polling marks success, reporting generation g loses desired g+1, missing state update strands a published head, or simultaneous publishers overwrite history. Green: all controls work against real remotes and all control-store providers; no force pushes; stale heads yield deterministic retries.
108	
109	## 11. Ph6: incoming integration, review, join migration and recovery
110	
111	Requirements: FR-MCP-178,180,181,186,187,188,189. Implement temporary integration branches, clean-merge validation, dirty-branch deferral, gated live-branch application, conflict review with head-bound resolution, recovery pins/receipts, maintenance preflight/attestation/status and derived-state refresh. Incoming data must not re-execute business commands or external effects. Include IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit, covering an isolated worker that must use the owning server's gate API.
112	
113	Classes: `FederationMergeReviewTests`, `FederationDirtyWorkingSetTests`, `FederationRecoveryTests`, `FederationEffectIsolationTests`. Cases include all-three concurrent nonconflicting commits, same-cell conflict, delete/update, invalid clean merge, missing ancestry, stale review, hub/node restart at each state transition, disconnect during upload, lost acknowledgement, concurrent resolution and unavailable derived indexes. Include OldSchemaUnpublishedCommitMergesAfterUpgrade, FeatureBranchSchemaCatchUp, DirtyDraftBlocksBinaryUpgrade and ContractBlockedUntilLocalBranchesAttested. The dirty-draft case proves the attempted swap is blocked and preserves the draft before schema merge. Preserve valid live data and all history; never report synchronized on conflict, dirty deferment or stale observation. Test older-schema node quarantine separately from network failure.
114	
115	After Ph4 commit/branch and Ph5 publication services exist, implement join mode here: clone C0, stage duplicate/legacy-divergence decisions, import J1, review/merge into M1, validate audit-backfill receipts and verify both J1 source accounting and M1 domain state before cutover readiness. Classes MigrationJoinTests and MigrationCutoverTests own MigrationJoinPreservesCommonAncestor, MigrationJoinDivergentRowRequiresReview and JoinCutoverRequiresReviewedMain. Ph3 did not claim these dependencies were available.
116	
117	Add ReviewAgeVisible, UnrelatedPublicationContinues, SafeTodoMergeRules and AuditBackfillVerified. Ph5 first owns HubRestoreFromOlderBackup for epoch/remote/control recovery; Ph6 extends that same contract through local merge, review and audit resend. It does not create a second owner or postpone the Ph5 case. Permit safe identical/independent-cell merges only under the explicit TODO policy. Preserve unresolved branch history and permit unrelated project/branch publication. The single writer sentence applies to live branches; worker integration refs use their narrower rights and every live move uses the owner's gate.
118	## 12. Ph7: server and plugin workflows
119	
120	Requirements: FR-MCP-183 and every workflow's plugin surface. Add typed DTO/client methods, REST/MCP/REPL adapters and equivalent audited plugin wrappers for installed first-party agents. Inventory actual plugin repositories and versions at phase entry; do not edit another plugin through the wrong agent identity. Expose capabilities, project/branch context, status/diff/history/commit/sync, branches, review, audit delivery status, identity enrollment/owner management, human-ID reservation, aliases, admin migration/export commands and maintenance.preflight/attest/status as defined by the architecture and TRs. Surface review/wait ages immediately, with15minute warning and24hour escalation in the operator inbox; no external messaging is sent automatically.
121	
122	Classes: `FederationClientContractTests`, `FederationMcpToolTests`, `FederationReplContractTests`, `FederationPluginConformanceTests`. Shared contract fixtures run against each plugin, including enrollment diagnostics, provenance/collision diagnostics, least-privilege denial, resume/status/cancel without false rollback, synchronization versus external effects, and editing-owner request/release/alternate-branch controls. Each obligation is explicit in the corresponding FR/TR/TEST, not inferred from a generic status command. Verify accurate local-committed/published/received status, unsupported-version errors, reconnect context revalidation, no implicit commits in turn hooks, real agent identity, normalized errors and safe cancellation. Human walkthrough uses the same service contracts as agents; no hidden raw-SQL path.
123	
124	## 13. Ph8: two-host acceptance, three-peer fixture and held cutover
125	
126	Build from the accepted integration SHA. Real-host acceptance requires LAB-OMARCHY(10.42.0.214/Linux) and PAYTON-LEGION2(10.42.0.143/Windows), both starting from retained SQLite copies. It does not depend on an unprovisioned third machine. Separately, Nuke provisions an ephemeral three-logical-peer fixture named FED-ATLAS-H, FED-ATLAS-A and FED-ATLAS-B with isolated databases, loopback dynamic ports and disposable roots under TestResults/{runId}; Ph0 proves that provisioning path on both OSs. These are test processes, never discovered hosts or production enrollment. Execute U01-U15; use H/A for real cross-link tests and the fixture for three-writer interleavings. Collect full requirements/AC/UC coverage and compare observed heads/rows/errors to the canonical GWT contracts.
127	
128	Ph8 owns the isolated real-host execution of DeploymentPreflightBlocksDirtyOrUnattestedBranch, WindowsWriterLockAndRestart, HubRestoreFromOlderBackup, SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink, UnknownCertificatePinRejected and ReceiptsAndLogsContainNoCredentials. Their implementation contracts remain owned by their earlier phase; HubRestoreFromOlderBackup first passes in Ph5 and is extended in Ph6. All B1-B12 evidence must include LEGION. An absent third physical host is not a blocker; absent fixture evidence is a failed gate.
129	
130	Ph8 uses disposable project data, isolated databases/ports and dedicated fixture roots on both real hosts. Existing unrelated lab work is not a substitute for isolated staging. For every applicable control, publication/history, audit and IdentityServer path, partition and reconnect the path independently; also exercise simultaneous A/B partitions in the three-peer fixture. Restart each application/worker, Dolt process, gateway, IdentityServer and control/audit store at the documented commit/publication/report boundaries. Compare captured branch heads, ancestor sets, refs, row values, retained drafts, audit delivery/receipts, secret exclusions and control outcomes before/after each fault. Record the matrix by host, component/path, fault, expected state, observed state and receipt. Network isolation must not disrupt unrelated projects.
131	
132	Collect all-four-provider regression and all-three-source migration receipts, reviewed join and all-domain recovery-export receipts, plus an actual isolated restore of the complete backup set. A missing component/path/provider row fails acceptance; neither unit mocks nor an empty queue substitute for these receipts. RealHostAcceptanceMatrix covers this requirement. Review-age, cancellation and plugin diagnostics use the same isolated scenarios. Live cutover remains a separate action under DEPLOY HOLD.
133	Before live cutover, inventory and back up both current lab hosts' provider databases, identity/configuration, legacy queue/fanout/conflicts and unpublished data. Run the migration planner on every participating legacy project. Designate one seed per ProjectId; every other source uses the clone-plus-delta join path, preserving common ancestry. Resolve identity collisions and pending legacy operations explicitly; do not drop them or run both legacy replay and Dolt publication for the same project. Verify target snapshots before switching. Keep federation disabled until this gate passes and the concrete cutover is approved under the operator's deployment policy. Approval records the verified all-domain/all-branch recovery manifest and operational backup/restore receipts. Cut over one host first, observe a 48-hour soak with successful offline/reconnect, audit delivery and recovery-export checks, then authorize the second host.
134	
135	DEPLOY HOLD remains active until the operator explicitly lifts it for this exact rollout. Plan approval, historical 98/98 or test success is not that release. Deploy through Nuke using the Linux container/native Windows package choices, protected configuration and persistent storage. Its deploy target calls maintenance preflight and refuses the binary swap on any dirty or unattested branch; it consumes the maintenance epoch/readiness receipt. SSH to LEGION2 as kingd using the configured authorized key. Enable only accepted projects; verify local operations before first publication, then enable subscriptions and polling. Cutover approval names planned join downtime from source quiescence through reviewed integration. Final acceptance includes one hub-authored commit and one commit from each node, both branch and conflict workflows, offline commits, and verified source retention. Stop after validation/reporting; do not extend into PR features or unrelated worktree cleanup.
136	
137	## 14. Traceability, review and readiness
138	
139	The [current-scope coverage index](2026-11-10-federation-reconciliation.md) identifies applicable requirements recovered from the gap check. The workflow inventory maps the 16 release contracts to phases, U01-U15 and 99 named acceptance cases. [Current implementation contracts and acceptance](2026-11-10-federation-current-contracts.md) includes the canonical schemas, endpoints, error codes and full Given/When/Then outcomes once in the PDF. Test names alone are not acceptance coverage. Keep existing IDs and update their current text rather than creating competing requirements. Export canonical requirements through the supported plugin, preserving unrelated working-tree changes; never regenerate an entire root file from a partial federation slice. Each substantive review amendment is persisted through the MCP plugin, read back and exported before phase exit. Historical source copies and unrelated obligations are not required plan reading or phase-exit work.
140	
141	Before a phase exits, every applicable AC must have executable evidence and every implemented workflow must satisfy its preconditions, success and failure paths. ValidateTraceability checks the FR/TR/TEST links. All amended criteria remain pending until the implementation passes the defined gates.
142	
143	Independent HV by an agent family other than the author targets accuracy and completeness of at least 98 each on the exact current architecture, plan, workflow and contract packet. This revision awaits that review and Ph0 feasibility evidence. Record source/PDF hashes and findings separately from the plan. DEPLOY HOLD requires explicit operator release after acceptance; neither plan approval nor a review score releases it.
144	### Review history and evidence boundaries
145	
146	Historical Claude rounds R1-R4 scored accuracy/completeness 89/84, 95/94, 97/97 and 98/98 (AGREE on the original six-file packet). Full request/response/verdict receipts are retained under docs/receipts/hv/20261110-federation-dolt-r{1..4}.*. R1-R3 tracked F01-F15, N1-N11, R3-M1 and R3-L1-L5; the receipt findings, not the scores alone, establish what was reviewed. R4-L1 is now covered by Ph7 maintenance surfaces and Ph8 deployment preflight; R4-L2 by the live-branch writer rule and restricted integration-worker rights. Those are author dispositions, not a fresh reviewer acceptance.
147	
148	The historical reviewer saw an isolated approved packet, lacked live operator decisions, builds/tests and browsing, and did not review the compiled PDF. The recorded runtime model was claude-opus-5-5; high effort was requested but not independently verified. Review infrastructure incidents are recorded separately from substantive scores. Historical final hashes/readback and the original 45-state visualization receipt remain evidence of that old packet only. The original 48-record create and first-update receipts were successful; later reconciliation amended 62 LAB records and restored six, and amended 20 LEGION records. These historical persistence counts are not current acceptance counts.
149	
150	The supplied revision audit compared the original 76-page PDF with the 48-page revision: 15 findings addressed, two partial, plus lost obligations and new inconsistencies. Its report and this revision's item-by-item dispositions are retained as receipts. The earlier source-to-PDF checks could not prove preservation of obligations removed from the source. This revision requires both a retention/disposition check and PDF inclusion checks. The exact original 39-page PDF remains unavailable; no comparison to that artifact is claimed.
151	
152	Future independent HV must receive the exact current source packet, rendered PDF and embedded-source hashes, the applicable operator decisions and audit dispositions, with full secret-safe request/response receipts. It must separately assess restored content and contradictions; old 98/98 cannot transfer to a new packet. No HV is launched or passed merely by editing this plan.

# Dolt federation: BDPv4 implementation plan

Author: Codex. Date: 2026-11-10. Status: proposed planning baseline; implementation readiness remains gated by Ph0 evidence. Independent review results are retained under docs/receipts/hv. No implementation, package installation, schema migration, data migration or federation activation has occurred.

Architecture authority: [Dolt federation architecture](2026-11-10-federation-dolt-architecture.md). Workflow evidence and requirement inventory: [three-system walkthrough](2026-11-10-federation-three-system-workflows.md). This plan replaces the old forwarding/read-switch execution sequence for versioned federation. Retain the October and earlier November drafts as historical evidence, not competing instructions.

## 1. Scope and acceptance

The logical peers H, A and B must independently edit and commit the same logical project's data, exchange committed histories through the hub, preserve uncommitted work and branches, and review conflicts without pull requests. Add Dolt as a fourth supported database and provide a safe migration tool from SQLite, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. Existing providers and explicit DirectProxy remain supported. The second node is the isolated FED-ATLAS-B test peer; real-host acceptance uses LAB and LEGION, with the three-peer fixture provisioned in Ph0.

Success is demonstrated by every workflow U01-U15, every linked FR/TR/TEST criterion, all supported provider regressions and three-system restart/recovery tests. An empty control table is insufficient proof: compare accepted commit ancestry, project data and branch state, including pending drafts/reviews. Source-code Git, arbitrary file synchronization, PRs, automatic hub election, live cross-provider CDC and concurrent independent schema migrations are outside this release.

## 2. Fastest dependency sequence

Phase identifiers are Ph0 through Ph8; they do not denote priority levels.

1. Ph0: prove Dolt/EF10/provider/remote fit before investing in integration.
2. Ph1: add fourth provider and separate schema migration assembly; preserve original providers.
3. Ph2: split project-versioned and operational storage, branch-scoped access and editing ownership.
4. Ph3: deliver seed migration, audit-backfill preparation and verified all-domain project recovery export; keep targets isolated.
5. Ph4: expose explicit commits, branch/history/diff and local publication intent.
6. Ph5: implement enrollment, guarded remote publication and the hub table/poller.
7. Ph6: implement safe receiving, reviewed merges, join migration and end-to-end crash/restore recovery.
8. Ph7: expose complete client/MCP/REPL/plugin workflows and user-visible status.
9. Ph8: run two-real-host acceptance plus a named three-logical-peer fixture, then prepare a staged lab cutover under DEPLOY HOLD.

Prepare test fixtures, DTO/API documentation and plugin contract fixtures during earlier phases where independent, but do not move unfinished implementation past a Byrd gate. Provider feasibility, not old forwarding fixes, is now the critical path. Reuse existing identity, diagnostics, provider abstractions, audit and typed clients; replace forwarding/command-replay paths only for versioned projects.

## 3. Source-control and donor handling

Create an isolated integration worktree from the current accepted develop when implementation is authorized. Suggested branch `integration/federation-dolt-20261110`; use separate small phase PRs against it. Preserve all existing worktrees and unrelated working-tree edits. Do not create or clean worktrees merely to write this plan.

The prior PR83/P1.5 work is a donor only for applicable security, identity, cross-platform path and regression fixes. Verify each current diff and test before porting. Do not merge old backfill, forwarding, read-switch or custom database synchronization machinery wholesale. C4 p4/*, namespace/analyzer work and historical worktree cleanup are not dependencies. Preserve explicit existing legacy modes through their named regression contracts; they do not authorize LocalProxy forwarding for versioned projects.

## 4. Byrd gate contract

For each small slice, first define the acceptance cases, fixtures and negative controls. Prove tests pass against controlled mocks and fail against deliberately wrong behavior. Then run the same contract against the missing/incorrect real implementation to record red, implement the smallest behavior, and refactor to green. Mocks must not simply return the expected result without testing the orchestration boundary.

Use targeted `./build.ps1 TestGroups --test-groups '<project>:<class>' --test-run-id '<phase-slice>'` after changes. At each phase exit run the entire current-plus-prior unit suite once with `./build.ps1 Test`, requiring zero failures and zero skips. `./build.ps1 Compile` and `./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability` are mandatory gate commands. Add real-container integration tests where a mock cannot prove SQL, migration, locking or remote semantics. Do not broaden/repeat a passing gate without changes or new evidence requiring it. Receipts include SHA/tree state, image/package versions, commands, TRX, fail/skip counts, AC mapping and negative controls.

The proposed test-class names below are implementation targets, not claims they exist today. Register new projects/classes in Nuke discovery as part of their owning phase. Do not add skipped placeholders for later phases; keep deferred coverage in requirements/TODO state.

Retain the operator's complete phase-exit gate on both LAB and LEGION: Nuke Test, MigrationIntegrationTests, the full Build.Tests suite, and ValidateTraceability at the same accepted head. Test currently excludes Build.Tests; do not infer its coverage from a green Test receipt. Ph0 records the complete discovered Build.Tests class inventory and its Nuke TestGroups invocation; every listed class and test must execute, with zero failures and zero skips. MigrationIntegrationTests and the new TestFederationProviders suite are complementary and neither replaces the other. Keep unit, integration and build-suite receipts distinct and run the full set once per final phase head, repeating only after changes or failed gates.

Add Nuke target `TestFederationProviders` with the planned command `./build.ps1 TestFederationProviders --providers sqlite,postgresql,sqlserver,dolt --test-run-id '<phase>-providers'`. It is not an existing command today. Ph0 records exact PostgreSQL/SQL Server/Dolt image versions and digests and the SQLite package version; Ph1 implements the target and refuses missing/unhealthy containers as a gate failure, never a skip. Every Ph1-Ph8 exit requires both the full unit gate and this real-provider/remote suite with zero failures and zero skips. Container-dependent classes are registered only in TestFederationProviders and excluded from Test by category at discovery, never runtime skipping. Receipts include image digests and environment readiness evidence.

## 5. Ph0: feasibility and exact dependency selection

Deliver a version-pinned compatibility receipt and license/dependency record for Dolt and the MySQL-protocol EF provider and driver selected under B1. Use current net10.0/EF10.0.0 as the baseline. Read the dependency compliance rules before additions. Existing Dolt EF samples establish possibility, not compatibility.

Prove on LAB Linux and LEGION native Windows against real databases (containers where appropriate): full current model creation; representative CRUD/LINQ/raw SQL; concurrency tokens; transaction rollback; decimal/date/text/index/FK mappings; migrations; branch connection isolation; explicit SQL commit versus Dolt commit; merge conflicts/constraints; clean and dirty remote pushes; lost responses; authenticated project isolation; inability to bypass guarded publication through raw remote requests. Verify canonical-ref advancement and remote recovery under process death. Compare candidate clean merges against domain validators.

Classes: `DoltProviderCompatibilityTests`, `DoltRemoteAuthorizationTests`, `DoltBranchIsolationTests`, `DoltCommitBoundaryTests`. Red conditions: unsupported mappings/query translation, ordinary SaveChanges creating history, pool branch leakage, unauthorized ref mutation or missing recovery guarantees. Green: all named contracts pass on pinned versions, no ad hoc provider fork or custom merge engine.

Ph0 runs a disposable harness and records exact commands, digests, TRX and fail/skip counts. Ph1 carries the proven Ph0 contract assertions into maintained classes under TestFederationProviders and passes them at Ph1 exit. If Ph0 changes repository code, the full Test gate also applies at Ph0 exit; disposable prototypes do not become an undocumented production dependency.

Ph0 exit consists of the following numbered **blocking outputs**. The implementation owner produces each evidence record; the operator accepts it, with independent HV by an agent family other than the author, assessing substantive accuracy/completeness. Each record stores owner, status (unproven/proven/accepted), evidence paths and dependent phases. Initial status for all B1-B12 is unproven. Every B1-B12 receipt has separate LAB and LEGION evidence rows; Windows is not inferred from Linux. Ph0 verifies the current-scope coverage index and binds each applicable acceptance criterion and workflow to its implementation phase. All must be accepted before Ph1 production integration begins; Ph0 prototypes remain disposable.

1. B1: exact provider/driver/image versions, digests, licenses and all-four-provider fixture versions; LAB /var/lib/dolt mount and native LEGION hosting inventory. Verify actual Windows service name/account/executable/start/recovery policy, data ACLs and child-process lifecycle before accepting the proposed host. If absent or unsuitable, obtain approval for a concrete supported alternative (Ph1-Ph8).
2. B2: every entity, relationship, interactive/automatic writer and auto-updated column; session capture remains operational and only explicit promoted snapshots become versioned (Ph2-Ph8).
3. B3: full standalone McpDbContext versus Dolt-only project/control context topology, additive migration chains and cross-database soft-reference validators (Ph1-Ph3).
4. B4: exact ID grammar per generated/human-assigned family, legacy compatibility, sort/display, parser/plugin/traceability changes and restored allocator behavior (Ph2-Ph8).
5. B5: exact restored Duende 7.4 patch version and matching source-tag/API references, with issuance/introspection/revocation tests on that package (v8 documentation is insufficient); existing IdentityServer client-per-node/owner binding, reference tokens and scopes, gateway introspection/revocation, backend-only Dolt credentials, enforceable remote publication permissions and credential containment, worker-only remote procedures, gated worker live-branch mutation path and rotation/revocation (Ph2/Ph5-Ph8).
6. B6: real merge/constraint/conflict-transaction semantics, retained review evidence, safe conflict persistence including whether `dolt_allow_commit_conflicts` is needed, and unrelated-history behavior. Never enable unresolved conflicts on live project branches (Ph4-Ph6).
7. B7: single-author schema distribution, startup migration exclusion, expand/contract rules, mandatory pre-binary-swap draft disposition, all-local-branch attestation/fencing, offline old-schema commits and feature catch-up, worker protocol negotiation (Ph1/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6/Ph8).
