B8: seed/join/recovery-export manifest, audit backfill, duplicate detection and permanent aliases, one common root, mandatory legacy-divergence review over B2-classified versioned columns after canonical normalization; reviewed scoped rules may expand to enumerated per-row decisions with no wildcard default. Include identity/deletion accounting, canonical hashes, immutable migration-commit plus final-main verification and closed-until-integrated cutover (Ph3 seed/export, Ph6 join, Ph8 acceptance).
9. B9: single writer ownership, write gate/fence transitions including every worker live-branch mutation, working-set hash API, requestId commit trailers and crash reconciliation (Ph2/Ph4-Ph6).
10. B10: measured fixture-scale storage/latency/history growth, resource budgets and explicit operating limits; no unsupported throughput/SLA claim (Ph1/Ph5/Ph8).
11. B11: polling/retry/stale-branch and15minute/24hour review-age thresholds, subscription-state schema and monotonic generation/epoch semantics (Ph5/Ph7).
12. B12: local/remote candidate/review refs, GC/retention, hub-restore epoch/reconciliation, network loopback isolation, named CA/pins and secret-safe receipts, plus secret-detection and disclosure response (Ph4-Ph8).

If a maintained EF10-compatible provider is unavailable, report concrete options for approval; do not downgrade the repository silently. This plan is executable through Ph0 but is not implementation-ready for later slices until these evidence-dependent choices are locked.

## 6. Ph1: fourth provider and schema migrations

Requirements: FR-MCP-186. Extend `McpDatabaseProviderKind`, `McpDatabaseProviderFactory`, `McpDbContextFactory`, runtime options/configuration validation, health output and setup tooling with canonical `dolt`. Add `DoltMcpDatabaseProviderStrategy` and `QBrainAi.Storage.DoltMigrations`, with provider-specific snapshot/baseline. Never edit existing migrations; add migrations only where B3 requires. Include provider selections in build/package/admin surfaces. Exclude versioned project databases from automatic startup migration; standalone/control contexts retain their approved migration path.

Classes: `DoltProviderResolutionTests`, `DoltMigrationTests`, `FourProviderContractTests`. Include VersionedProjectNotMigratedAtStartup in this owning phase. First prove unknown-provider rejection, unchanged defaults and distinct migration assembly selection. Real-provider tests cover empty database creation, baseline-to-next upgrade, interrupted startup/retry, idempotent reapplication, schema drift detection and application CRUD after upgrade. Test all original providers for regression. No production data copy in this phase.

## 7. Ph2: project routing, data boundaries and editing ownership

Requirements: FR-MCP-174,176,177,182,184,185,189. Add immutable ProjectId/local-path enrollment mapping, per-project provider selection, project and control contexts, full table classification, branch-scoped DbContext/query/index keys, local ID allocation and fenced edit leases. A versioned project's ordinary requests must never enter LocalProxy forwarding. Preserve DirectProxy behavior for explicit legacy configuration; no ambiguous combination on one project.

Fold MCP-FEDIDENTITY-001 owner binding and user-management requirements into this phase. Audit/outbox storage remains unversioned, but its delivery obligation is hub-bound, not local-only. Define scoped permanent aliases and local provisional IDs; host paths and credentials remain local. Classes: `FederationLocalExecutionTests`, `ProjectBranchContextTests`, `FederationDataBoundaryTests`, `NodeTaggedIdentityTests`, `BranchEditLeaseTests`. Cases include BackgroundWritersDoNotDirtyVersionedBranch, SecondAgentLoggingNeedsNoLease, LegacyIdsRemainValid and LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected. Red: offline request waits for hub, cross-project row visible, secret or branchable audit in clone, duplicate IDs after branch/restart, pooled connection changes branch, or one agent commits another's work. Green: local read-after-write/restart, complete entity/writer classification, no branch/project leakage, safe expired-lease recovery and stable replicated IDs. Provider schema changes introduced here require migrations for each affected supported provider, not Dolt alone.

LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected means admission after expiry/fence change is rejected and takeover waits for an already-admitted transaction; it does not demand aborting a transaction legitimately holding the gate through completion.

## 8. Ph3: seed migration and project recovery export

Requirements: FR-MCP-187, FR-MCP-182/184, FR-MCP-AUDIT-001 and the reconciled backfill contracts. Implement the shared migration planner, immutable source manifest, duplicate-candidate review, permanent alias mapping, seed-only run/resume/verify/status/abort and frozen-head Dolt-to-new-SQLite project export. Audit backfill preparation accounts for every historical TODO/generic audit row; actual hub delivery/receipt binding joins Ph5. Ph3 never invokes publication or reviewed join functionality that does not yet exist.

Classes: MigrationPlannerTests, MigrationResumeTests, MigrationIdentityMappingTests, MigrationVerificationTests, ThreeProviderToDoltMigrationTests, TodoRecoveryExportTests and ProjectRecoveryExportTests. Reuse TEST-MCP-235's exact Given/When/Then cases. SeedPhaseRejectsJoin returns HTTP 501 unsupported_capability with no writes when mode=join is requested. ThreeSourceProviderRoundTrip covers SQLite,PostgreSQL,SQL Server fixtures; both live lab sources are SQLite. DoltTodoExportPreservesNewWrites proves a post-cutover TODO and its child/link/alias graph survive export while retained source bytes remain unchanged. FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains additionally proves every versioned domain, unpublished branch and dirty working set survives per-branch SQLite export plus the retained Dolt archive; operational stores are backed up at the same quiescence boundary and audit is reconciled. A missing domain or branch blocks routing changes. Same-work/different-ID candidates require review; never rewrite historical text references.

Migration acceptance also covers multi-project separation, soft-deleted rows, decimal/UTC/binary/Unicode edge cases, complete promoted session graphs, hub-bound audit, derived-index rebuild and inert imported operational records. Inject death after target batch commit before acknowledgement, before provider switch and after switch before reopening. Dry-run and failed verification must preserve source bytes and active routing. Ph6 applies the same matrix to joins; source accounting and reviewed-main verification are separate checks.

Exit: disposable seed migrations and verified recovery exports pass all four-provider gates. Keep source SQLite snapshots read-only. No live cutover, join commit, public-ref update or source deletion occurs. Join-specific cases remain planned for Ph6, not skipped tests in Ph3.
## 9. Ph4: explicit history commits and local publication intent

Requirements: FR-MCP-175,177,183,184,189. Implement status/diff/history/commit preview, idempotent explicit commit, branch lifecycle and local unpublished-head scanning. No save hook implicitly creates Dolt history. A hub request cannot auto-commit drafts. Protect preview fingerprints, author provenance and branch edit ownership.

Classes: `FederationCommitTests`, `FederationBranchLifecycleTests`, `PublicationIntentRecoveryTests`. Include CommitRetryReturnsSameHash, CommitPreviewBlocksSecret and StaleBranchReportedNotDeleted. Red: edits trigger sync, commit bundles unauthorized changes, restart loses an unreported commit, or fetched remote commits cause endless republishing. Green: durable explicit commit triggers exactly the needed sync intent, history reconstruction repairs crash windows without duplicate commits, feature publication does not merge main.

## 10. Ph5: hub control table and publication

Requirements: FR-MCP-176,178,179,181,182,184,185. Provision the hub shared remote separately from its local working copy. Implement enrollment and project/branch subscription, candidate upload/validation/acceptance, expected-head publication, SyncSubscription state-table migrations, polling/reporting, durable receipts, worker epochs and remote-head reconciliation. One row per subscription replaces command-message generations/leases/coalescing. Both nodes initiate communication; H's local worker uses the same authenticated gateway. Add existing IdentityServer clients/scopes, audit/batches ingestion with idempotent receipts, human-ID reservation, restore epoch and polling. Test AuditReachesHub, AuditRetryIdempotent, SimultaneousHumanIdReservation, SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink and HubRestoreFromOlderBackup. No native remote endpoint is exposed to node credentials.

Classes: `FederationEnrollmentTests`, `FederationPublicationTests`, `FederationControlTableTests`, `FederationPollingTests`. Include LocalAppUserCannotPush, RevokedCredentialFailsFetchAndPublish and OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess. Red: node can publish unauthorized branch/project, hub drafts block publication, polling marks success, reporting generation g loses desired g+1, missing state update strands a published head, or simultaneous publishers overwrite history. Green: all controls work against real remotes and all control-store providers; no force pushes; stale heads yield deterministic retries.

## 11. Ph6: incoming integration, review, join migration and recovery

Requirements: FR-MCP-178,180,181,186,187,188,189. Implement temporary integration branches, clean-merge validation, dirty-branch deferral, gated live-branch application, conflict review with head-bound resolution, recovery pins/receipts, maintenance preflight/attestation/status and derived-state refresh. Incoming data must not re-execute business commands or external effects. Include IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit, covering an isolated worker that must use the owning server's gate API.

Classes: `FederationMergeReviewTests`, `FederationDirtyWorkingSetTests`, `FederationRecoveryTests`, `FederationEffectIsolationTests`. Cases include all-three concurrent nonconflicting commits, same-cell conflict, delete/update, invalid clean merge, missing ancestry, stale review, hub/node restart at each state transition, disconnect during upload, lost acknowledgement, concurrent resolution and unavailable derived indexes. Include OldSchemaUnpublishedCommitMergesAfterUpgrade, FeatureBranchSchemaCatchUp, DirtyDraftBlocksBinaryUpgrade and ContractBlockedUntilLocalBranchesAttested. The dirty-draft case proves the attempted swap is blocked and preserves the draft before schema merge. Preserve valid live data and all history; never report synchronized on conflict, dirty deferment or stale observation. Test older-schema node quarantine separately from network failure.

After Ph4 commit/branch and Ph5 publication services exist, implement join mode here: clone C0, stage duplicate/legacy-divergence decisions, import J1, review/merge into M1, validate audit-backfill receipts and verify both J1 source accounting and M1 domain state before cutover readiness. Classes MigrationJoinTests and MigrationCutoverTests own MigrationJoinPreservesCommonAncestor, MigrationJoinDivergentRowRequiresReview and JoinCutoverRequiresReviewedMain. Ph3 did not claim these dependencies were available.

Add ReviewAgeVisible, UnrelatedPublicationContinues, SafeTodoMergeRules and AuditBackfillVerified. Ph5 first owns HubRestoreFromOlderBackup for epoch/remote/control recovery; Ph6 extends that same contract through local merge, review and audit resend. It does not create a second owner or postpone the Ph5 case. Permit safe identical/independent-cell merges only under the explicit TODO policy. Preserve unresolved branch history and permit unrelated project/branch publication. The single writer sentence applies to live branches; worker integration refs use their narrower rights and every live move uses the owner's gate.
## 12. Ph7: server and plugin workflows

Requirements: FR-MCP-183 and every workflow's plugin surface. Add typed DTO/client methods, REST/MCP/REPL adapters and equivalent audited plugin wrappers for installed first-party agents. Inventory actual plugin repositories and versions at phase entry; do not edit another plugin through the wrong agent identity. Expose capabilities, project/branch context, status/diff/history/commit/sync, branches, review, audit delivery status, identity enrollment/owner management, human-ID reservation, aliases, admin migration/export commands and maintenance.preflight/attest/status as defined by the architecture and TRs. Surface review/wait ages immediately, with15minute warning and24hour escalation in the operator inbox; no external messaging is sent automatically.

Classes: `FederationClientContractTests`, `FederationMcpToolTests`, `FederationReplContractTests`, `FederationPluginConformanceTests`. Shared contract fixtures run against each plugin, including enrollment diagnostics, provenance/collision diagnostics, least-privilege denial, resume/status/cancel without false rollback, synchronization versus external effects, and editing-owner request/release/alternate-branch controls. Each obligation is explicit in the corresponding FR/TR/TEST, not inferred from a generic status command. Verify accurate local-committed/published/received status, unsupported-version errors, reconnect context revalidation, no implicit commits in turn hooks, real agent identity, normalized errors and safe cancellation. Human walkthrough uses the same service contracts as agents; no hidden raw-SQL path.

## 13. Ph8: two-host acceptance, three-peer fixture and held cutover

Build from the accepted integration SHA. Real-host acceptance requires LAB-OMARCHY(10.42.0.214/Linux) and PAYTON-LEGION2(10.42.0.143/Windows), both starting from retained SQLite copies. It does not depend on an unprovisioned third machine. Separately, Nuke provisions an ephemeral three-logical-peer fixture named FED-ATLAS-H, FED-ATLAS-A and FED-ATLAS-B with isolated databases, loopback dynamic ports and disposable roots under TestResults/{runId}; Ph0 proves that provisioning path on both OSs. These are test processes, never discovered hosts or production enrollment. Execute U01-U15; use H/A for real cross-link tests and the fixture for three-writer interleavings. Collect full requirements/AC/UC coverage and compare observed heads/rows/errors to the canonical GWT contracts.

Ph8 owns the isolated real-host execution of DeploymentPreflightBlocksDirtyOrUnattestedBranch, WindowsWriterLockAndRestart, HubRestoreFromOlderBackup, SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink, UnknownCertificatePinRejected and ReceiptsAndLogsContainNoCredentials. Their implementation contracts remain owned by their earlier phase; HubRestoreFromOlderBackup first passes in Ph5 and is extended in Ph6. All B1-B12 evidence must include LEGION. An absent third physical host is not a blocker; absent fixture evidence is a failed gate.

Ph8 uses disposable project data, isolated databases/ports and dedicated fixture roots on both real hosts. Existing unrelated lab work is not a substitute for isolated staging. For every applicable control, publication/history, audit and IdentityServer path, partition and reconnect the path independently; also exercise simultaneous A/B partitions in the three-peer fixture. Restart each application/worker, Dolt process, gateway, IdentityServer and control/audit store at the documented commit/publication/report boundaries. Compare captured branch heads, ancestor sets, refs, row values, retained drafts, audit delivery/receipts, secret exclusions and control outcomes before/after each fault. Record the matrix by host, component/path, fault, expected state, observed state and receipt. Network isolation must not disrupt unrelated projects.

Collect all-four-provider regression and all-three-source migration receipts, reviewed join and all-domain recovery-export receipts, plus an actual isolated restore of the complete backup set. A missing component/path/provider row fails acceptance; neither unit mocks nor an empty queue substitute for these receipts. RealHostAcceptanceMatrix covers this requirement. Review-age, cancellation and plugin diagnostics use the same isolated scenarios. Live cutover remains a separate action under DEPLOY HOLD.
Before live cutover, inventory and back up both current lab hosts' provider databases, identity/configuration, legacy queue/fanout/conflicts and unpublished data. Run the migration planner on every participating legacy project. Designate one seed per ProjectId; every other source uses the clone-plus-delta join path, preserving common ancestry. Resolve identity collisions and pending legacy operations explicitly; do not drop them or run both legacy replay and Dolt publication for the same project. Verify target snapshots before switching. Keep federation disabled until this gate passes and the concrete cutover is approved under the operator's deployment policy. Approval records the verified all-domain/all-branch recovery manifest and operational backup/restore receipts. Cut over one host first, observe a 48-hour soak with successful offline/reconnect, audit delivery and recovery-export checks, then authorize the second host.

DEPLOY HOLD remains active until the operator explicitly lifts it for this exact rollout. Plan approval, historical 98/98 or test success is not that release. Deploy through Nuke using the Linux container/native Windows package choices, protected configuration and persistent storage. Its deploy target calls maintenance preflight and refuses the binary swap on any dirty or unattested branch; it consumes the maintenance epoch/readiness receipt. SSH to LEGION2 as kingd using the configured authorized key. Enable only accepted projects; verify local operations before first publication, then enable subscriptions and polling. Cutover approval names planned join downtime from source quiescence through reviewed integration. Final acceptance includes one hub-authored commit and one commit from each node, both branch and conflict workflows, offline commits, and verified source retention. Stop after validation/reporting; do not extend into PR features or unrelated worktree cleanup.

## 14. Traceability, review and readiness

The [current-scope coverage index](2026-11-10-federation-reconciliation.md) identifies applicable requirements recovered from the gap check. The workflow inventory maps the 16 release contracts to phases, U01-U15 and 99 named acceptance cases. [Current implementation contracts and acceptance](2026-11-10-federation-current-contracts.md) includes the canonical schemas, endpoints, error codes and full Given/When/Then outcomes once in the PDF. Test names alone are not acceptance coverage. Keep existing IDs and update their current text rather than creating competing requirements. Export canonical requirements through the supported plugin, preserving unrelated working-tree changes; never regenerate an entire root file from a partial federation slice. Each substantive review amendment is persisted through the MCP plugin, read back and exported before phase exit. Historical source copies and unrelated obligations are not required plan reading or phase-exit work.

Before a phase exits, every applicable AC must have executable evidence and every implemented workflow must satisfy its preconditions, success and failure paths. ValidateTraceability checks the FR/TR/TEST links. All amended criteria remain pending until the implementation passes the defined gates.

Independent HV by an agent family other than the author targets accuracy and completeness of at least 98 each on the exact current architecture, plan, workflow and contract packet. This revision awaits that review and Ph0 feasibility evidence. Record source/PDF hashes and findings separately from the plan. DEPLOY HOLD requires explicit operator release after acceptance; neither plan approval nor a review score releases it.
### Review history and evidence boundaries

Historical Claude rounds R1-R4 scored accuracy/completeness 89/84, 95/94, 97/97 and 98/98 (AGREE on the original six-file packet). Full request/response/verdict receipts are retained under docs/receipts/hv/20261110-federation-dolt-r{1..4}.*. R1-R3 tracked F01-F15, N1-N11, R3-M1 and R3-L1-L5; the receipt findings, not the scores alone, establish what was reviewed. R4-L1 is now covered by Ph7 maintenance surfaces and Ph8 deployment preflight; R4-L2 by the live-branch writer rule and restricted integration-worker rights. Those are author dispositions, not a fresh reviewer acceptance.

The historical reviewer saw an isolated approved packet, lacked live operator decisions, builds/tests and browsing, and did not review the compiled PDF. The recorded runtime model was claude-opus-5-5; high effort was requested but not independently verified. Review infrastructure incidents are recorded separately from substantive scores. Historical final hashes/readback and the original 45-state visualization receipt remain evidence of that old packet only. The original 48-record create and first-update receipts were successful; later reconciliation amended 62 LAB records and restored six, and amended 20 LEGION records. These historical persistence counts are not current acceptance counts.

The supplied revision audit compared the original 76-page PDF with the 48-page revision: 15 findings addressed, two partial, plus lost obligations and new inconsistencies. Its report and this revision's item-by-item dispositions are retained as receipts. The earlier source-to-PDF checks could not prove preservation of obligations removed from the source. This revision requires both a retention/disposition check and PDF inclusion checks. The exact original 39-page PDF remains unavailable; no comparison to that artifact is claimed.

Future independent HV must receive the exact current source packet, rendered PDF and embedded-source hashes, the applicable operator decisions and audit dispositions, with full secret-safe request/response receipts. It must separately assess restored content and contradictions; old 98/98 cannot transfer to a new packet. No HV is launched or passed merely by editing this plan.

1	# Three-system federation walkthrough and requirements
2	
3	Author: Codex. Date: 2026-11-10. Proposed behavior for [the new architecture](2026-11-10-federation-dolt-architecture.md), not a report of deployed behavior. H=LAB-OMARCHY, A=PAYTON-LEGION2, B=isolated test peer FED-ATLAS-B. Project Atlas and symbolic commit names C0/A1/B1/H1/M1 are examples, not real records or hashes. The hub has a local working copy and a separate shared committed-history remote.
4	
5	## Standard workflows
6	
7	### U01: enroll and start the same project
8	
9	H registers Atlas with immutable ProjectId and an initial approved C0. A and B enroll with distinct immutable node tags, map their own filesystem paths to Atlas, receive authorized subscriptions and clone C0. Each can now read and edit locally. An existing nonempty node database is inventoried/migrated, never overwritten by the clone. Server: enrollment, project identity, initial snapshot, scoped credentials. Plugins: discover/select project and branch; show local/remote heads. Requirements: FR-MCP-176,182,185,187.
10	
11	### U02: node A edits, then commits
12	
13	A edits a TODO. Its local draft survives restart, but H and B remain at C0 and no sync is triggered. A previews and explicitly commits A1; this wakes synchronization. After validated publication, the hub remote is A1 and H/B receive control requests. Their workers fetch and accept A1 on clean branches; their local reads now include the TODO. Server: explicit commits, publication and control generation. Plugins: diff/commit/status; distinguish local commit from publication. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,179,183,189.
14	
15	### U03: work directly on the hub
16	
17	H edits in its local working copy while A and B continue independently. H commits H1 and its normal worker publishes it to the shared remote; A/B receive requests. H's uncommitted draft before H1 neither travels nor prevents A/B publication because the hub remote is a separate repository. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,184.
18	
19	### U04: simultaneous clean edits on all three systems
20	
21	Starting at C0, A commits a title edit A1, B commits an unrelated description edit B1, and H commits a separate requirement H1. A publishes first. B fetches A1, Dolt merges A1+B1 into M1, validation passes and M1 publishes. H fetches M1, merges H1 into M2 and publishes. A/B accept M2. Every original commit remains an ancestor. A publication race returns head_changed and repeats fetch/merge; no force push. This assumes nonconflicting cells and valid domain relationships. Requirements: FR-MCP-178,181,188.
22	
23	### U05: conflicting edits to the same field
24	
25	A and B both change one requirement's priority from the same base to different values and commit independently. A publishes A1. B receives A1 while holding B1; merge reports a conflict. B retains its last valid local state, and H/A retain A1. B's plugin displays base/local/incoming values and requests review. A reviewed resolution creates M1 including both histories, passes validation and publishes; H/A then accept it. Changed heads invalidate an old resolution. Delete/update and schema conflicts use the same visible review boundary. Requirements: FR-MCP-180,181,183.
26	
27	### U06: hub unreachable, then reconnect
28	
29	The A/B-to-hub link fails; H retains local access to its own gateway and remote. H, A and B still execute local business operations and make H1/A1/B1 commits. H may publish H1 locally while A/B record pending publication; they do not return queued-only results for local business writes. On reconnect A merges H1+A1 into M1 and publishes, then B merges M1+B1 into M2 and publishes; H/A catch up to M2. They authenticate, reconcile remote heads and process requests plus their own unpublished commits. Merge/review follows U04/U05. An empty hub queue does not strand local commits. No automatic hub failover is claimed. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,179,181,185.
30	
31	### U07: incoming commit while node B has a draft
32

Phase: Ph4. Workflows: U02, U07, U09. Tests: SaveDoesNotPublish; VersionCommitTriggersSync; HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft; OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart.

### FR-MCP-176: logical project enrollment and initial clone

Nodes enroll a logical project under immutable shared identity while retaining host-local paths and refusing destructive clones.

Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.

Phase: Ph2/Ph5. Workflows: U01. Tests: DifferentHostPathsSameProject; CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget; UnauthorizedProjectDenied; PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics.

### FR-MCP-177: branches across server and plugin context

First-release project branches support isolated work, explicit sharing and reviewed merge; session selection never leaks between connections.

Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U08, U12. Tests: PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch; FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged; BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads.

### FR-MCP-178: bidirectional committed-history exchange

Exchange committed history bidirectionally through guarded publication, preserving every accepted ancestor and the hub independent working copy.

Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U03, U04, U08. Tests: ThreeWriterCleanConvergence; HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote; ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories.

### FR-MCP-179: hub control table and polling

Use a durable hub subscription table with polling, generation and worker fencing, plus a fresh hub epoch after restore.

Phase: Ph5. Workflows: U02, U06, U09, U15. Tests: PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge; AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest; MissedNotificationReconciles; HubRestoreFromOlderBackup.

### FR-MCP-180: reviewed conflicts and valid merges

Conflicts and invalid merges preserve valid live data, require authorized review and remain visible with ageing while unrelated publication continues.

Phase: Ph6/Ph7. Workflows: U05, U07, U08. Tests: SameCellConflictNeedsReview; DeleteUpdateNeedsReview; CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation; StaleReviewRejected; ReviewAgeVisible; UnrelatedPublicationContinues; SafeTodoMergeRules.

### FR-MCP-181: recovery without lost or repeated work

Recover synchronization, receipts and restored hub state without losing local work, inventing success or replaying business effects.

Server: durable operation resume/status/safe cancellation. Plugin: expose resume, status and cancel with completed-versus-pending effects; never claim cancellation reverses published history.

Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U06, U07, U09, U15. Tests: LostPushAckDoesNotDuplicateCommit; OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess; DirtyBranchDefersApply; IncompatibleSchemaDoesNotApply; PluginRecoveryControls.

### FR-MCP-182: collision-resistant and preserved identity

Prevent generated-ID collisions, preserve permanent legacy aliases, detect duplicate work and atomically reserve human-assigned IDs.

Server: provenance, scoped aliases, collision evidence and reservation outcomes. Plugin: expose provenance/collision diagnostics and the authorized resolution path without rewriting historical references.

Phase: Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U01, U10, U14. Tests: TwoNodesCreateDistinctIds; BranchRevertDoesNotReuseSequence; LegacyCollisionPreservesReferences; LegacyIdsRemainValid; DifferentIdsSameTodoDetected; SimultaneousHumanIdReservation; OfflineHumanIdPublicationDenied; PluginIdentityDiagnostics.

### FR-MCP-183: first-party plugin federation contract

Expose consistent typed federation, review, identity, audit, migration and maintenance workflows through every first-party plugin.

Phase: Ph4/Ph7. Workflows: U01, U02, U05, U07, U08, U11, U12, U13, U14, U15. Tests: EveryPluginUsesSameContract; OldServerReportsUnsupportedCapability; ReconnectRevalidatesContext; StaleBranchReportedNotDeleted.

### FR-MCP-184: portable data versus host-local state

Separate versioned project content from operational state while delivering permanent audit to the hub independently of commits and excluding secrets.

Phase: Ph2/Ph3/Ph4/Ph5/Ph6/Ph7. Workflows: U10, U13. Tests: CloneOmitsSecrets; AuditReachesHub; AuditRetryIdempotent; AuditBackfillVerified; FullProjectSessionGraphPreserved; AcceptedHeadRebuildsBranchIndex; BackgroundWritersDoNotDirtyVersionedBranch; SecondAgentLoggingNeedsNoLease; CommitPreviewBlocksSecret; ReceiptsAndLogsContainNoCredentials.

### FR-MCP-185: scoped authorization and offline behavior

Reuse integrated IdentityServer for single-user node ownership, per-node client credentials, project scopes and revocation; preserve authorized offline work.

Server: least-privilege capabilities plus server-side authorization on every call. Plugin: show available rights and explicit denial; capability display never substitutes for authorization.

Phase: Ph0/Ph2/Ph5. Workflows: U01, U06, U13. Tests: RawRemoteCannotBypassPublicationPolicy; ForeignProjectCloneDenied; RevokedNodeCannotPublish; OfflineLocalAuthorizationStillApplies; LocalAppUserCannotPush; RevokedCredentialFailsFetchAndPublish; SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink; UnknownCertificatePinRejected; PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial.

### FR-MCP-186: Dolt fourth-provider support and schema migration

Support Dolt as the fourth provider with dedicated schema migration, controlled schema-history distribution, Windows/Linux lifecycle and original-provider regressions.

Phase: Ph0/Ph1/Ph6/Ph8. Workflows: U11. Tests: FourProvidersResolve; DoltBaselineAndUpgrade; OriginalProviderMigrationsUnchanged; UnsupportedSchemaRejected; VersionedProjectNotMigratedAtStartup; OldSchemaUnpublishedCommitMergesAfterUpgrade; FeatureBranchSchemaCatchUp; DirtyDraftBlocksBinaryUpgrade; ContractBlockedUntilLocalBranchesAttested; DeploymentPreflightBlocksDirtyOrUnattestedBranch; WindowsWriterLockAndRestart; RealHostAcceptanceMatrix.

### FR-MCP-187: original-provider-to-Dolt migration tool

Migrate all three original providers using verified seed then reviewed join, permanent identities, audit backfill and a source-retaining all-domain/all-branch project-to-SQLite recovery export.

Phase: Ph3 seed/export; Ph6 join. Workflows: U10, U14. Tests: ThreeSourceProviderRoundTrip; ResumeAfterBatchCommit; ChangedSnapshotRejected; FailedVerifyCannotCutover; SourceRetainedAfterCutover; MigrationJoinPreservesCommonAncestor; MigrationJoinDivergentRowRequiresReview; JoinCutoverRequiresReviewedMain; DoltTodoExportPreservesNewWrites; SeedPhaseRejectsJoin; FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains.

### FR-MCP-188: imported state does not repeat external effects

Imported project or audit state never replays external effects and general federation remains outside QuadBrain-only keyserver gating.

Server: synchronization applies data without executing external operations. Plugin: distinguish history/data synchronization from separately authorized external effects in preview, status and receipts.

Phase: Ph2/Ph6. Workflows: U04, U09, U13. Tests: ImportDoesNotSendExternalAction; RetryDoesNotRepeatEffect; ImportedOperationalRowsRemainInert; FederationBypassesQuadBrainKeyserver; PluginEffectBoundary.

### FR-MCP-189: safe shared-host editing and commit ownership

Enforce branch edit ownership and fenced live-write serialization so no agent or sync worker captures or overwrites another agent draft.

Server: editing owner, request/release and fenced takeover contracts. Plugin: display editing owner, request/release context and offer another branch without capturing another agent draft.

Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U07, U12. Tests: CommitCannotCaptureOtherAgentDraft; ExpiredLeaseFenced; PreviewChangeRequiresReview; LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected; CommitRetryReturnsSameHash; IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit; PluginEditingOwnership.

## Planning boundaries

The operator requested Dolt support and the migration tool; no packages or deployments are authorized by this document alone. Exact provider/version compatibility and full entity partition remain Ph0 evidence gates. The table/poller/executor, plugin UX and validation are application work; the Dolt storage/history/merge algorithms are reused. PRs remain out of scope. Test names above are required behavior, not claims of existing or passing tests.

The new-contract slice retains its48 IDs and 16 mappings; the reconciliation register additionally covers legacy and cross-cutting requirements from both hosts. Each HV revision updates existing FR/TR/TEST records through the plugin and refreshes the export before Ph0 exit; no duplicate requirement set is created.

1	# Three-system federation walkthrough and requirements
2	
3	Author: Codex. Date: 2026-11-10. Proposed behavior for [the new architecture](2026-11-10-federation-dolt-architecture.md), not a report of deployed behavior. H=LAB-OMARCHY, A=PAYTON-LEGION2, B=isolated test peer FED-ATLAS-B. Project Atlas and symbolic commit names C0/A1/B1/H1/M1 are examples, not real records or hashes. The hub has a local working copy and a separate shared committed-history remote.
4	
5	## Standard workflows
6	
7	### U01: enroll and start the same project
8	
9	H registers Atlas with immutable ProjectId and an initial approved C0. A and B enroll with distinct immutable node tags, map their own filesystem paths to Atlas, receive authorized subscriptions and clone C0. Each can now read and edit locally. An existing nonempty node database is inventoried/migrated, never overwritten by the clone. Server: enrollment, project identity, initial snapshot, scoped credentials. Plugins: discover/select project and branch; show local/remote heads. Requirements: FR-MCP-176,182,185,187.
10	
11	### U02: node A edits, then commits
12	
13	A edits a TODO. Its local draft survives restart, but H and B remain at C0 and no sync is triggered. A previews and explicitly commits A1; this wakes synchronization. After validated publication, the hub remote is A1 and H/B receive control requests. Their workers fetch and accept A1 on clean branches; their local reads now include the TODO. Server: explicit commits, publication and control generation. Plugins: diff/commit/status; distinguish local commit from publication. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,179,183,189.
14	
15	### U03: work directly on the hub
16	
17	H edits in its local working copy while A and B continue independently. H commits H1 and its normal worker publishes it to the shared remote; A/B receive requests. H's uncommitted draft before H1 neither travels nor prevents A/B publication because the hub remote is a separate repository. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,184.
18	
19	### U04: simultaneous clean edits on all three systems
20	
21	Starting at C0, A commits a title edit A1, B commits an unrelated description edit B1, and H commits a separate requirement H1. A publishes first. B fetches A1, Dolt merges A1+B1 into M1, validation passes and M1 publishes. H fetches M1, merges H1 into M2 and publishes. A/B accept M2. Every original commit remains an ancestor. A publication race returns head_changed and repeats fetch/merge; no force push. This assumes nonconflicting cells and valid domain relationships. Requirements: FR-MCP-178,181,188.
22	
23	### U05: conflicting edits to the same field
24	
25	A and B both change one requirement's priority from the same base to different values and commit independently. A publishes A1. B receives A1 while holding B1; merge reports a conflict. B retains its last valid local state, and H/A retain A1. B's plugin displays base/local/incoming values and requests review. A reviewed resolution creates M1 including both histories, passes validation and publishes; H/A then accept it. Changed heads invalidate an old resolution. Delete/update and schema conflicts use the same visible review boundary. Requirements: FR-MCP-180,181,183.
26	
27	### U06: hub unreachable, then reconnect
28	
29	The A/B-to-hub link fails; H retains local access to its own gateway and remote. H, A and B still execute local business operations and make H1/A1/B1 commits. H may publish H1 locally while A/B record pending publication; they do not return queued-only results for local business writes. On reconnect A merges H1+A1 into M1 and publishes, then B merges M1+B1 into M2 and publishes; H/A catch up to M2. They authenticate, reconcile remote heads and process requests plus their own unpublished commits. Merge/review follows U04/U05. An empty hub queue does not strand local commits. No automatic hub failover is claimed. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,179,181,185.
30	
31	### U07: incoming commit while node B has a draft
32	
33	B has uncommitted edits at C0. A publishes A1; B polls and fetches history, but records waiting_local_work instead of committing, discarding or overwriting its draft. B's user finishes the draft and explicitly commits B1 (or separately chooses another authorized disposition). Then reconciliation proceeds. Fetch succeeded does not mean the branch was synchronized. Requirements: FR-MCP-175,180,183,189.
34	
35	### U08: divergent feature work and deliberate merge
36	
37	A creates feature/search from C0 and commits F1. Publication shares feature/search; main remains C0 on all systems. B selects feature/search to inspect or continue it and commits F2. H can review the branch data. An authorized explicit merge into main creates M1 and triggers normal publication. Branch selection is per session, never a process-wide switch. No PR is created. Requirements: FR-MCP-177,180,183,189.
38	
39	### U09: lost response or crash during synchronization
40	
41	A publishes A1 but loses the success response. H has A1 and unsatisfied subscription state. A restarts, checks remote ancestry and its request receipt, and recognizes publication without creating A2 or repeating an external business action. A missed hub state update is repaired by head-generation reconciliation. A new worker epoch rejects stale reports from the old worker. Reporting generation g must not clear desired g+1. Requirements: FR-MCP-179,181,188.
42	
43	### U10: migrate an existing project
44	
45	Both real lab stores are SQLite. The migration tool additionally supports PostgreSQL and SQL Server fixture sources. It plans those sources, inventories local-only versus shared data, detects legacy-ID collisions and checks the Dolt schema. Ph3 delivers seed and all-domain/all-branch project recovery export (including the TODO subset); Ph6 adds join only after branch/commit/publication/review exist. Exactly one seed establishes C0 per project. Other nodes clone C0 and import their frozen legacy differences on migration branches descended from C0, then merge/review them normally. Verification accounts for source rows already in C0, mapped deltas and explicitly reviewed exclusions/deletions. Include TODO/generic audit history in the independent hub backfill and verify every durable receipt. Detect same-work/different-ID duplicates for review and preserve permanent origin-scoped aliases, without rewriting historical text. A failed verification leaves the original provider active. No unrelated root histories or implicit deletion of seed rows are allowed. Requirements: FR-MCP-182,184,186,187.
46	
47	Same-identity rows with different legacy contents require a recorded keep-seed/take-join/manual-value review before the join commit, even if Dolt would merge cleanly. Verify the immutable migration commit and the reviewed main result; keep destination writes closed until integration and verification finish.
48	
49	### U11: node running an older schema/application
50	
51	H's maintenance role publishes a supported schema upgrade. B advertises an older capability and records incompatible_schema; it does not apply it or claim to be current. B may continue supported local work while publication is held. After preflight and binary upgrade, B merges S1 with its retained unpublished B1 to form M1, validates and publishes M1, then H/A accept M1. Both B1 and S1 remain ancestors; B does not simply replace B1 with S1. Each feature branch catches up separately through review/validation. Nodes never independently run EF migrations on versioned project startup. Incompatible contract changes wait for subscriber acknowledgement or explicit de-enrollment/recovery. Requirements: FR-MCP-181,183,186.
52	
53	Before swapping B's binary, its owners explicitly commit or resolve all drafts and the schema head must be available locally; otherwise upgrade waits without touching drafts. B attests every local branch, including unpublished ones. Maintenance preflight gates deployment. Each branch reopens only after its local worker merges the designated schema history and validation passes; a catch-up conflict blocks that branch only. The new EF model never edits an unsupported dirty working set or independently executes project migrations.
54	
55	### U12: two agents on one host
56	
57	Two plugins select Atlas/main on A. Only the editing lease owner may mutate its working set. The other agent reads or selects a separate branch. The first agent's commit preview binds to its expected working-set fingerprint; takeover cannot silently absorb its draft. Plugin reconnect revalidates the lease and context. Requirements: FR-MCP-177,183,189.
58	
59	### U13: audit reaches the hub without a project commit
60	
61	Precondition: A is enrolled in Atlas; main=C0 and A has authorized local audit storage. A edits T1 while offline, appending immutable audit E1 and its outbox entry. On reconnect, audit/batches sends E1 through the IdentityServer gateway, independent of Dolt commits. The hub stores it append-only and returns a hash-bound receipt. A lost receipt causes retry, not duplication; the node retains E1 permanently. Postcondition: one E1 at each origin/hub ledger, main and remote still C0, local draft preserved. Errors: invalid_token, unauthorized_project, audit_id_conflict. Requirements: FR-MCP-AUDIT-001, FR-MCP-184/185/188. Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph7.
62	
63	### U14: duplicate work, permanent aliases and human IDs
64	
65	Precondition: frozen LAB TODO-7 and LEGION TODO-91 describe the same task. Planning emits similarity evidence; it does not infer identity automatically. An authorized review chooses keep-both or one canonical entity with both scoped IDs retained as aliases. Historical commits, PRs, session logs, memories and documents remain unchanged. For new human labels, two concurrent reservations of IMPL-UNITGREEN-001 yield one owner and one human_id_reserved response. Offline work uses a tagged provisional ID until reservation succeeds. Postcondition: every old reference remains resolvable with origin context, no unreviewed row disappears, and an ambiguous unqualified ID reports ambiguous_legacy_id. Requirements: FR-MCP-182/187. Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6.
66	
67	### U15: restore a hub older than a node
68	
69	Precondition: A1 was published under epoch E1/generation90 and remains on A/B, but the backup contains C0/generation40. Restore keeps ingress disabled, installs a fresh E2 and advertises only verified restored heads. A node's E1 report receives hub_epoch_changed; it retains A1. The hub requests candidate history and validates ancestry before republishing A1 under E2. Audit inventories reconcile independently and permanent node ledgers resend missing records. Postcondition: no force push or forced node rewind, all recovered history preserved, receipts refer to E2 and no missing audit row is falsely acknowledged. Requirements: FR-MCP-179/181/184/188. Ph5/Ph6/Ph8.
70	
71	## UC preconditions, success and exception coverage
72	
73	U01 starts with authenticated owner/node enrollment and empty target; succeeds with shared C0 and distinct local paths; nonempty/foreign target is denied. U02 starts with editable C0; succeeds with explicit A1 and eventual peer acceptance; draft or failed publication remains local. U03 is U02 on H with a separate shared remote. U04 starts at common C0 and three distinct edits; succeeds at M2 preserving H1/A1/B1/M1; conflict takes U05. U05 starts with same-base conflicting commits; succeeds only at an authorized valid merge; stale preview is rejected. U06 starts with enrolled peers and link loss; succeeds after M1/M2 reconciliation without queued-only local writes. U07 starts with a dirty B branch; succeeds only after the owner explicitly disposes the draft and merge validates; waiting age remains visible. U08 starts with C0 and authorized feature creation; sharing leaves main unchanged and explicit merge creates M1. U09 starts with an accepted commit and lost reply; retry returns the same hash/receipt without replay. U10 starts with retained frozen sources; success requires seed/join accounting, reviewed aliases, audit receipts and verified main; any failed verify blocks cutover. U11 starts with an unsupported incoming schema and unpublished work; success preserves B1 plus S1 ancestry after preflight and M1 validation; dirty/unattested branches block upgrade. U12 starts with agent1's edit lease; agent2 reads or selects another branch; no commit captures agent1's draft. U13-U15 state their own preconditions/postconditions above. Exact row/head/error assertions are canonical TEST-MCP-222..237 criteria, not inferred from diagram labels.
74	## New requirement and feature inventory
75	
76	The IDs below are the intended canonical records; the registration receipt establishes whether persistence succeeded. Status is pending throughout. Each FR maps one-to-one in order to TR-MCP-FEDERATION-001..016 and TEST-MCP-222..237. This inventory is additive; conflicting legacy-mode descriptions require explicit reconciliation, not blanket deletion.
77	
78	### FR-MCP-174: autonomous local execution
79	
80	Every node, including the hub, performs authorized local business operations and persists results without hub connectivity.
81	
82	Phase: Ph2. Workflows: U02, U03, U06. Tests: NodeWorksWithHubUnavailable; HubUsesSameLocalExecution; OfflineLocalReadAfterWrite.
83	
84	### FR-MCP-175: explicit version commits and publication boundary
85	
86	Only an explicit version-history commit triggers publication; drafts and SQL saves remain local. Commit retries recover the same history identity.
87	
88	Phase: Ph4. Workflows: U02, U07, U09. Tests: SaveDoesNotPublish; VersionCommitTriggersSync; HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft; OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart.
89	
90	### FR-MCP-176: logical project enrollment and initial clone
91	
92	Nodes enroll a logical project under immutable shared identity while retaining host-local paths and refusing destructive clones.
93	
94	Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.
95	
96	Phase: Ph2/Ph5. Workflows: U01. Tests: DifferentHostPathsSameProject; CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget; UnauthorizedProjectDenied; PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics.
97	
98	### FR-MCP-177: branches across server and plugin context
99	
100	First-release project branches support isolated work, explicit sharing and reviewed merge; session selection never leaks between connections.
101	
102	Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U08, U12. Tests: PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch; FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged; BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads.
103	
104	### FR-MCP-178: bidirectional committed-history exchange
105	
106	Exchange committed history bidirectionally through guarded publication, preserving every accepted ancestor and the hub independent working copy.
107	
108	Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U03, U04, U08. Tests: ThreeWriterCleanConvergence; HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote; ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories.
109	
110	### FR-MCP-179: hub control table and polling
111	
112	Use a durable hub subscription table with polling, generation and worker fencing, plus a fresh hub epoch after restore.
113	
114	Phase: Ph5. Workflows: U02, U06, U09, U15. Tests: PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge; AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest; MissedNotificationReconciles; HubRestoreFromOlderBackup.
115	
116	### FR-MCP-180: reviewed conflicts and valid merges
117	
118	Conflicts and invalid merges preserve valid live data, require authorized review and remain visible with ageing while unrelated publication continues.
119	
120	Phase: Ph6/Ph7. Workflows: U05, U07, U08. Tests: SameCellConflictNeedsReview; DeleteUpdateNeedsReview; CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation; StaleReviewRejected; ReviewAgeVisible; UnrelatedPublicationContinues; SafeTodoMergeRules.
121	
122	### FR-MCP-181: recovery without lost or repeated work
123	
124	Recover synchronization, receipts and restored hub state without losing local work, inventing success or replaying business effects.
125	
126	Server: durable operation resume/status/safe cancellation. Plugin: expose resume, status and cancel with completed-versus-pending effects; never claim cancellation reverses published history.
127	
128	Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U06, U07, U09, U15. Tests: LostPushAckDoesNotDuplicateCommit; OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess; DirtyBranchDefersApply; IncompatibleSchemaDoesNotApply; PluginRecoveryControls.
129	
130	### FR-MCP-182: collision-resistant and preserved identity
131	
132	Prevent generated-ID collisions, preserve permanent legacy aliases, detect duplicate work and atomically reserve human-assigned IDs.
133	
134	Server: provenance, scoped aliases, collision evidence and reservation outcomes. Plugin: expose provenance/collision diagnostics and the authorized resolution path without rewriting historical references.
135	
136	Phase: Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U01, U10, U14. Tests: TwoNodesCreateDistinctIds; BranchRevertDoesNotReuseSequence; LegacyCollisionPreservesReferences; LegacyIdsRemainValid; DifferentIdsSameTodoDetected; SimultaneousHumanIdReservation; OfflineHumanIdPublicationDenied; PluginIdentityDiagnostics.
137	
138	### FR-MCP-183: first-party plugin federation contract
139	
140	Expose consistent typed federation, review, identity, audit, migration and maintenance workflows through every first-party plugin.
141	
142	Phase: Ph4/Ph7. Workflows: U01, U02, U05, U07, U08, U11, U12, U13, U14, U15. Tests: EveryPluginUsesSameContract; OldServerReportsUnsupportedCapability; ReconnectRevalidatesContext; StaleBranchReportedNotDeleted.
143	
144	### FR-MCP-184: portable data versus host-local state
145	
146	Separate versioned project content from operational state while delivering permanent audit to the hub independently of commits and excluding secrets.
147	
148	Phase: Ph2/Ph3/Ph4/Ph5/Ph6/Ph7. Workflows: U10, U13. Tests: CloneOmitsSecrets; AuditReachesHub; AuditRetryIdempotent; AuditBackfillVerified; FullProjectSessionGraphPreserved; AcceptedHeadRebuildsBranchIndex; BackgroundWritersDoNotDirtyVersionedBranch; SecondAgentLoggingNeedsNoLease; CommitPreviewBlocksSecret; ReceiptsAndLogsContainNoCredentials.
149	
150	### FR-MCP-185: scoped authorization and offline behavior
151	
152	Reuse integrated IdentityServer for single-user node ownership, per-node client credentials, project scopes and revocation; preserve authorized offline work.
153	
154	Server: least-privilege capabilities plus server-side authorization on every call. Plugin: show available rights and explicit denial; capability display never substitutes for authorization.
155	
156	Phase: Ph0/Ph2/Ph5. Workflows: U01, U06, U13. Tests: RawRemoteCannotBypassPublicationPolicy; ForeignProjectCloneDenied; RevokedNodeCannotPublish; OfflineLocalAuthorizationStillApplies; LocalAppUserCannotPush; RevokedCredentialFailsFetchAndPublish; SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink; UnknownCertificatePinRejected; PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial.
157	
158	### FR-MCP-186: Dolt fourth-provider support and schema migration
159	
160	Support Dolt as the fourth provider with dedicated schema migration, controlled schema-history distribution, Windows/Linux lifecycle and original-provider regressions.
161	
162	Phase: Ph0/Ph1/Ph6/Ph8. Workflows: U11. Tests: FourProvidersResolve; DoltBaselineAndUpgrade; OriginalProviderMigrationsUnchanged; UnsupportedSchemaRejected; VersionedProjectNotMigratedAtStartup; OldSchemaUnpublishedCommitMergesAfterUpgrade; FeatureBranchSchemaCatchUp; DirtyDraftBlocksBinaryUpgrade; ContractBlockedUntilLocalBranchesAttested; DeploymentPreflightBlocksDirtyOrUnattestedBranch; WindowsWriterLockAndRestart; RealHostAcceptanceMatrix.
163	
164	### FR-MCP-187: original-provider-to-Dolt migration tool
165	
166	Migrate all three original providers using verified seed then reviewed join, permanent identities, audit backfill and a source-retaining all-domain/all-branch project-to-SQLite recovery export.
167	
168	Phase: Ph3 seed/export; Ph6 join. Workflows: U10, U14. Tests: ThreeSourceProviderRoundTrip; ResumeAfterBatchCommit; ChangedSnapshotRejected; FailedVerifyCannotCutover; SourceRetainedAfterCutover; MigrationJoinPreservesCommonAncestor; MigrationJoinDivergentRowRequiresReview; JoinCutoverRequiresReviewedMain; DoltTodoExportPreservesNewWrites; SeedPhaseRejectsJoin; FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains.
169	
170	### FR-MCP-188: imported state does not repeat external effects
171	
172	Imported project or audit state never replays external effects and general federation remains outside QuadBrain-only keyserver gating.
173	
174	Server: synchronization applies data without executing external operations. Plugin: distinguish history/data synchronization from separately authorized external effects in preview, status and receipts.
175	
176	Phase: Ph2/Ph6. Workflows: U04, U09, U13. Tests: ImportDoesNotSendExternalAction; RetryDoesNotRepeatEffect; ImportedOperationalRowsRemainInert; FederationBypassesQuadBrainKeyserver; PluginEffectBoundary.

178	### FR-MCP-189: safe shared-host editing and commit ownership
179	
180	Enforce branch edit ownership and fenced live-write serialization so no agent or sync worker captures or overwrites another agent draft.

182	Server: editing owner, request/release and fenced takeover contracts. Plugin: display editing owner, request/release context and offer another branch without capturing another agent draft.
183	
184	Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U07, U12. Tests: CommitCannotCaptureOtherAgentDraft; ExpiredLeaseFenced; PreviewChangeRequiresReview; LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected; CommitRetryReturnsSameHash; IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit; PluginEditingOwnership.

# Federation current-scope coverage

This index covers the new Dolt federation release. The architecture, phase plan and U01-U15 workflows define scope. Earlier plans were consulted to recover applicable requirements; their original text and unrelated requirements are not part of this plan.

## Release contracts and acceptance criteria

FR-MCP-174 through 189 map in order to TR-MCP-FEDERATION-001 through 016 and TEST-MCP-222 through 237. The workflow inventory names each contract, its phase, workflows and acceptance tests. Together these define 99 current Given/When/Then cases. The [current contract and acceptance specification](2026-11-10-federation-current-contracts.md) includes the full schemas, endpoint/error contracts and Given/When/Then criteria once in this packet, with canonical FR/TR/TEST IDs. Applicable gap-check criteria and the migration fixture matrix are included there too. All criteria remain pending implementation evidence.

U01-U15 cover enrollment, local/hub commits, concurrent work, conflicts, disconnect/reconnect, drafts, branches, retries, migration, schema upgrades, multiple agents, audit delivery, duplicate identity and hub restore. Their preconditions, steps, success outcomes and exception paths are in the workflow document. Ph0 registers these workflows in the UC store and binds their requirement links; no pre-existing federation UC was found in either queried workspace.

## Applicable requirements recovered by the gap check

- **Autonomous execution and compatibility:** FR-MCP-103, TR-MCP-FED-001 and TEST-MCP-136 now require local execution with committed-history exchange. FR-MCP-077 preserves existing explicitly selected DirectProxy behavior as a regression boundary. Ph2/Ph5; FR-MCP-174/178/185.
- **Permanent audit reaches the hub:** FR-MCP-AUDIT-001, TR-MCP-AUDIT-002/003/004 and TEST-MCP-AUDIT-001/002/003 cover append-only storage, protected runtime permissions, secret exclusion, delivery receipts and migration backfill. Ph2/Ph3/Ph5; FR-MCP-184/187.
